'''Juan Martín del Potro''' ({{IPA|es|xwam<!--assimilation to following /m/; see [[Help:IPA/Spanish]]--> maɾˈtin del ˈpotɾo}};<ref>{{cite web |title=The pronunciation by Juan Martín del Potro himself |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/-/media/player-names/64_juanmartin-delpotro_player-name-2014.mp3 |publisher=ATP World Tour |access-date=22 October 2017 |archive-date=28 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170128130910/http://www.atpworldtour.com/-/media/player-names/64_juanmartin-delpotro_player-name-2014.mp3 |url-status=live}}</ref> born 23 September 1988) is an Argentine former professional [[tennis]] player.<ref name="retirement">{{cite web |title=Emotional Juan Martin del Potro announces retirement from tennis |url=https://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/ATP_Tennis/108853/emotional-juan-martin-del-potro-announces-retirement-from-tennis/ |access-date=5 February 2023 |website=Tennis World USA|date=5 February 2022}}</ref> He was ranked world No. 3 in men's singles by the [[Association of Tennis Professionals]] (ATP), in August 2018. Del Potro won 22 [[ATP Tour]]-level singles titles, including a [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|major]] at the [[2009 US Open – Men's singles|2009 US Open]], where he defeated [[Rafael Nadal]] and the five-time defending champion [[Roger Federer]] en route. Del Potro's other career highlights include storming to the [[2018 US Open – Men's singles|2018 US Open]] final, winning an Olympic silver medal at the [[Tennis at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|2016 Rio Olympics]] and a bronze medal at the [[Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|2012 London Olympics]], winning [[Indian Wells Masters|Indian Wells]] in [[2018 BNP Paribas Open – Men's singles|2018]], and leading [[Argentina Davis Cup team|Argentina]] to the [[2016 Davis Cup]] title.

Del Potro first quietly entered the top 10 of the [[ATP rankings]] on 6 October 2008. With his US Open win, he became the only man outside the [[Big Three (tennis)|Big Three]] (Nadal, Federer, and [[Novak Djokovic]]) to win a major between the [[2005 French Open – Men's singles|2005 French Open]] and the [[2012 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles|2012 Wimbledon Championships]], a span of 30 tournaments.<ref name="USO final">{{cite web |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2009/09/US-Open-Final-Federer-del-Potro.aspx |title=Del Potro absolutely stuns Federer to win title |publisher=ATP World Tour |date=14 September 2009 |access-date=4 October 2009 |author=ATP Staff |archive-date=22 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090922215150/http://www.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2009/09/US-Open-Final-Federer-del-Potro.aspx |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2016, del Potro led Argentina to its first [[Davis Cup]] title by defeating Croatia's [[Marin Čilić]] in the final from two sets down. He then reached his first major semifinal in four years by defeating Federer in 4 sets in the quarterfinals of the [[2017 US Open – Men's singles|2017 US Open]]. In 2018, he won his first [[ATP Masters 1000]] title at Indian Wells, defeating the defending champion and world No. 1 Federer in the final. After reaching the semifinals of the [[2018 French Open – Men's singles|2018 French Open]], he matched his career-high ranking of No. 4, and in August 2018 he reached the world No. 3 ranking for the first time. At the 2018 US Open, he reached his second major final, where he lost to Djokovic. 
Notably, his career was hampered by a succession of wrist and knee injuries. Del Potro did not play between June 2019 and February 2022 because of pain from a knee injury, formally retiring in 2024 after a farewell exhibition match against Djokovic.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://batimes.com.ar/news/sports/tearful-juan-martin-del-potro-breaks-down-on-court-as-retirement-nears.phtml |title=Tearful Juan Martín del Potro breaks down on court as retirement nears |work=[[Buenos Aires Times]] |publisher=Editorial Perfil S.A |date=8 February 2022 |access-date=9 February 2022 |archive-date=9 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209022134/https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/sports/tearful-juan-martin-del-potro-breaks-down-on-court-as-retirement-nears.phtml |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="retirement" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/On_the_ATP_results_with/150247/juan-martin-del-potro-beats-novak-djokovic-and-ends-his-career/ |title=Juan Martin del Potro beats Novak Djokovic and ends his career |date=2 December 2024}}</ref>{{TOC limit|3}}

==Early life==
Juan Martín del Potro was born in [[Tandil]], Argentina. His father, Daniel del Potro (1957–2021), played [[rugby union]] in Argentina and was a [[veterinarian]].<ref name="Town of Red Meat and Tennis">{{cite news |last=Bishop |first=Greg |title=Town of Red Meat and Tennis Raises Another Star |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/09/08/sports/tennis/08delpotro.html?_r=1 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=7 September 2009 |access-date=14 September 2009 |archive-date=31 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231175200/http://www.nytimes.com/2009/09/08/sports/tennis/08delpotro.html?_r=1 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Przybylski |first=Mariano |url=http://www.revista-noticias.com.ar/comun/nota.php?art=1670&ed=1661 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081028001755/http://www.revista-noticias.com.ar/comun/nota.php?art=1670&ed=1661 |url-status=dead |archive-date=28 October 2008 |title=Trama secreta de la final |work=Revista Noticias |access-date=24 August 2009 |language=es}}</ref> His mother, Patricia Lucas, is a teacher, and he has a younger sister named Julieta. He also had an elder sister, who died in a car accident when she was eight years old.<ref name="independent.co.uk">{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/juan-martin-del-potro-to-win-first-you-have-to-know-how-to-lose-2286506.html |title=Juan Martin del Potro: 'To win, first you have to know how to lose' | Profiles | News |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |access-date=11 March 2016 |archive-date=19 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171119054017/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/juan-martin-del-potro-to-win-first-you-have-to-know-how-to-lose-2286506.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Del Potro speaks Spanish, English and some Italian.<ref name="ATP Profile">{{cite news |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/Tennis/Players/Top-Players/Juan-Martin-Del-Potro.aspx |title=ATP World Tour profile |publisher=ATP World Tour |access-date=14 September 2009 |archive-date=6 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150606020905/http://www.atpworldtour.com/Tennis/Players/Top-Players/Juan-Martin-Del-Potro.aspx |url-status=live}}</ref>

Aside from tennis, he enjoys playing association football and supports the [[Boca Juniors]] team in Argentina and [[Juventus]] in Italy.<ref name="ATP Profile"/> He would often dedicate time to both sports during his youth, and Argentine-Italian international footballer [[Mauro Camoranesi]], who grew up in the same town, remains a close friend of del Potro.<ref name="Town of Red Meat and Tennis"/>

Del Potro began playing tennis at the age of seven with coach Marcelo Gómez (who also coached Tandil-born players [[Juan Mónaco]], [[Mariano Zabaleta]] and [[Máximo González]]).<ref name="Town of Red Meat and Tennis"/> Del Potro's talent was discovered by Italian ex-tennis professional [[Ugo Colombini]], who accompanied him through the initial phases of his young career, and is still today his agent and close friend.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://deniksport.blesk.cz/clanek/tenis-davis-cup/76963/del-potro-nici-soupere-jako-sampras.html |title=Del Potro ničí soupeře. Jako Sampras |publisher=Denik Sport |date=10 July 2009 |access-date=21 August 2009 |language=cs |archive-date=20 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620042809/https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/tenis-davis-cup/76963/del-potro-nici-soupere-jako-sampras.html |url-status=live}}</ref> When questioned in 2007 about his ambitions in tennis he replied, "I dream of winning a Grand Slam and the Davis Cup."<ref name="Del Potro ready to make giant leap"/> Despite refusing to participate in the Davis Cup several times, he has since achieved both goals.

==Tennis career==

===Junior years===
Del Potro played his first junior match in April 2003 at the age of 14 at a Grade-2 tournament in Italy. As a junior in 2002, del Potro won the [[Junior Orange Bowl (tennis)|Orange Bowl]] 14s title, beating [[Marin Čilić]] en route to a victory over Pavel Tchekov in the final.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clgandjrtennis.com/JrOrangeBowl02.htm |title=2002 Junior Orange Bowl |publisher=College and Junior Tennis |access-date=28 September 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110708164313/http://www.clgandjrtennis.com/JrOrangeBowl02.htm |archive-date=8 July 2011 |df=dmy-all}}</ref> In 2003, at the age of 14, del Potro received [[Wild card (sports)#Professional tennis|wildcards]] to three [[International Tennis Federation|ITF Circuit]] events in Argentina, where he lost in [[Tennis terminology#S|straight sets]] in the first round of each.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/players/juan-martin-del-potro/d683/player-activity?year=2003 |title=Del Potro 2003 singles activity |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |access-date=16 September 2023}}</ref>

As a junior, del Potro reached as high as No. 3 in the combined ITF junior world rankings, in January 2005.<ref name="itfjunior">{{cite web |title=Juan Martin Del Potro Juniors singles overview |url=https://www.itftennis.com/en/players/juan-martin-del-potro/800247437/arg/jt/S/overview/ |publisher=International Tennis Federation (ITF)}}</ref>

===2004–2005: Early career===
In May 2004, del Potro won his first senior match, at the age of 15, at the ITF Circuit event in [[Buenos Aires]] by defeating Matias Niemiz. He then went on to lose in three sets to [[Sebastián Decoud]] in the second round. Del Potro saw his world ranking rise from No. 1441 in August to No. 1077 in November.<ref name="atp2004">{{cite web |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/players/juan-martin-del-potro/d683/player-activity?year=2004 |title=Del Potro 2004 singles activity |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |access-date=20 September 2023}}</ref> He also reached the finals in the Argentina Cup and [[Internazionali BNL d'Italia|Campionati Internazionali D'Italia]] Junior tournaments.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.wilsonracquet.net/juan-martin-del-potro-profile/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206125000/http://www.wilsonracquet.net/juan-martin-del-potro-profile/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=6 February 2022 |title=Juan Martin del Potro Profile |publisher=Wilson Tennis Racquets |access-date=17 September 2009}}</ref>

Del Potro reached his first final of the ITF Junior Circuit on 11 January 2005, the "Copa del Cafe (Coffee Bowl)" Junior ITF Tournament in Costa Rica, where he lost to [[Robin Haase]] in three sets. Because of the rain delays, the final set had to be played indoors; the first time the [[indoor courts]] had been used in the 44-year history of the youth tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nacion.com/puro-deporte/otros-deportes/a-del-potro-le-robaron-la-copa-del-cafe-del-2005/H3AQF5CV7ZBGNLRZ7HUCN6G2XA/story/ |title=A del Potro le robaron la Copa del Café del 2005 |work=Nacion.com |date=11 January 2005 |access-date=16 September 2023 |author=Harold Leandro C. |language=es}}</ref>

At the age of 16, del Potro reached his first senior singles final at the [[Futures tournaments|Futures tournament]] in Berimbau Naucalpan, Mexico, where he lost to [[Darko Mađarovski]]. He then went on to win consecutive titles at two Future ITF Circuit events in [[Santiago]], Chile, including the 26th International Junior tournament. In the first tournament, he beat [[Jorge Aguilar]], and in the second, he did not drop a set in the whole tournament and defeated [[Thiago Alves (tennis)|Thiago Alves]] in the final, a player ranked more than 400 places higher at the time. He won his third title in his home country by defeating [[Damián Patriarca]], who forfeited the match, at the ITF Circuit event in Buenos Aires.<ref name="atp2005">{{cite web |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/players/juan-martin-del-potro/d683/player-activity?year=2005 |title=Del Potro 2005 singles activity |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |access-date=20 September 2023}}</ref>

Del Potro turned professional in June 2005 and in his first professional tournament, the [[Lines Trophy]] Challenger tournament in [[Reggio Emilia]], he reached the semifinals, where he lost to countryman [[Martín Vassallo Argüello]] in three sets. Two tournaments later, he reached the final of the [[Credicard Citi MasterCard Tennis Cup]] in Campos do Jordão, Brazil where he lost to [[André Sá]] in straight sets. After turning 17, he won the [[ATP Montevideo|Montevideo Challenger]] by defeating [[Boris Pašanski]] in the final in three sets.<ref name="atp2005"/> That same year, he failed in his first attempt to [[2005 U.S. Open – Men's Qualifying Singles|qualify]] for his first major, at the [[2005 US Open – Men's singles|US Open]], losing in the first round to Paraguayan [[Ramón Delgado]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://stevegtennis.com/results/2005/q-a-usopen.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050924044933/http://stevegtennis.com/results/2005/q-a-usopen.txt |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 September 2005 |title=US Open qualifying August 29 – September 11, 2005 |publisher=Steve G Tennis |access-date=18 September 2009}}</ref> Throughout 2005, del Potro jumped over 900 positions to finish with a world ranking of No. 157, largely due to winning three Futures tournaments.<ref name="atp2005"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://stevegtennis.com/rankings/2005/s2005.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060509001256/http://stevegtennis.com/rankings/2005/s2005.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=9 May 2006 |title=Year End ATP Entry Rankings For 2005 |publisher=Steve G Tennis |access-date=28 September 2009}}</ref> He was the youngest player to finish in the year-end top 200.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/sports/2009-09/10/content_8676902.htm |title=Del Potro eyes final spot |work=China Daily |date=10 September 2009 |access-date=19 September 2009 |archive-date=23 November 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101123002453/http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/sports/2009-09/10/content_8676902.htm |url-status=live}}</ref>

===2006: Top 100===
In February, del Potro played his [[2006 Movistar Open – Singles|first ATP Tour event]] in Viña del Mar, where he defeated [[Albert Portas]], before losing to [[Fernando González]] in the second round.<ref name="Del Potro factfile">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/tennis/usopen/6192663/US-Open-2009-Juan-Martin-del-Potro-factfile.html |title=US Open 2009: Juan Martín del Potro factfile |work=The Telegraph |date=15 September 2009 |access-date=19 September 2009 |location=London |archive-date=23 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090923013703/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/tennis/usopen/6192663/US-Open-2009-Juan-Martin-del-Potro-factfile.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Later, seeded seventh, he won the Copa Club Campestre de Aguascalientes by defeating the likes of [[Dick Norman]] and [[Thiago Alves (tennis)|Thiago Alves]], before beating [[Sergio Roitman]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stevegtennis.com/results/2006/ch-aguascalientes.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060405041249/http://stevegtennis.com/results/2006/ch-aguascalientes.txt |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 April 2006 |title=Copa Club Campestre de Aguascalientes April 3–9, 2006 |publisher=Steve G Tennis |access-date=19 September 2009}}</ref><ref name="2006 Singles Activity">{{cite web |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/Tennis/Players/Top-Players/Juan-Martin-Del-Potro.aspx?t=pa&y=2006&m=s&e=0# |title=Del Potro 2006 Singles Activity |publisher=ATP World Tour |access-date=19 September 2009 |archive-date=12 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121012171152/http://www.atpworldtour.com/Tennis/Players/Top-Players/Juan-Martin-Del-Potro.aspx?t=pa&y=2006&m=s&e=0 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Del Potro qualified for the main draw of his first major in the [[2006 French Open – Men's singles|2006 French Open]] at the age of 17. He lost in the opening round to former French Open champion and 24th seed [[Juan Carlos Ferrero]].<ref name="2006 Singles Activity"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://stevegtennis.com/results/2006/a-frenchopen.txt |title=French Open May 29 – June 11, 2006 |publisher=Steve G Tennis |access-date=20 September 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090628050339/http://stevegtennis.com/results/2006/a-frenchopen.txt |archive-date=28 June 2009}}</ref> Having received a wildcard, he reached the quarterfinals of the [[Croatia Open Umag|ATP event]] in Umag, Croatia, where he lost in three sets to the eventual champion, [[Stanislas Wawrinka]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/Share/Event-Draws.aspx?e=439&y=2006 |title=ATP Studena Croatia Open July 24–30, 2006 |publisher=ATP World Tour |access-date=10 April 2013 |archive-date=16 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130516053902/http://www.atpworldtour.com/Share/Event-Draws.aspx?e=439&y=2006 |url-status=live}}</ref> In Spain, he participated in the [[Open Castilla y León]] Challenger tournament held in Segovia, defeating top seed [[Fernando Verdasco]] in the quarterfinals and [[Benjamin Becker]] in the final.<ref name="2006 Singles Activity"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://stevegtennis.com/results/2006/ch-segovia.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081011203502/http://stevegtennis.com/results/2006/ch-segovia.txt |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 October 2008 |title=Open Castilla y Leon – El Espinar July 31 – August 6, 2006 |publisher=Steve G Tennis |access-date=20 September 2009}}</ref>

Del Potro qualified for his first [[2006 US Open – Men's singles|US Open]] in 2006, where he lost in the first round to fellow qualifier [[Alejandro Falla]] of Colombia in four sets.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://stevegtennis.com/results/2006/a-usopen.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060901030355/http://stevegtennis.com/results/2006/a-usopen.txt |url-status=dead |archive-date=1 September 2006 |title=US Open August 28 – September 10, 2006 |publisher=Steve G Tennis |access-date=20 September 2009}}</ref> He qualified for his first [[ATP Masters Series]] tournament in Spain, the [[Mutua Madrileña Madrid Open|Madrid Open]], where he lost in the first round to [[Joachim Johansson]].<ref name="2006 Singles Activity"/> After receiving a wild card thanks to [[Roger Federer]], he reached the quarterfinals of the [[2006 Davidoff Swiss Indoors – Singles|2006 Swiss Indoors]] in Basel, defeating [[lucky loser]] [[Tobias Clemens]] in the first round and [[George Bastl]] in the second round, before losing to the eventual runner-up [[Fernando González]] in three sets.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/Share/Event-Draws.aspx?e=328&y=2006 |title=Davidoff Swiss Indoors – Basel 24–29 October 2006 |publisher=ATP World Tour |access-date=10 April 2013 |archive-date=22 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150422220843/http://www.atpworldtour.com/Share/Event-Draws.aspx?e=328&y=2006 |url-status=live}}</ref> Del Potro finished 2006 as the youngest player in the top 100, aged 18 years, 2 months.<ref name="ATP Profile"/>

|first=Diane |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-us-open15-2009sep15,0,9052.story |title=Juan Martin del Potro stuns Roger Federer to win U.S. Open |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=15 September and [[2021 US Open – Men's singles|2021]] champion [[Daniil Medvedev]].<ref>{{cite web dethrones Federer">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8253976.stm |title=Del Potro dethrones Federer in US |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 September 2009 |access-date=15 September [[Dick Enberg]] hosted the post-match ceremony, during which a victorious del Potro requested to address his fans in Spanish. Enberg declined the request, saying that he was running out of time, but went on to list the corporate sponsored prizes del Potro won.<ref name="straightsets">{{cite news |url=http://straightsets.blogs.nytimes.com/2009/09/15/can-i-speak-in-spanish/?scp=1&sq=can%20i%20speak%20spanish&st=cse |title=Can I Speak in Spanish? |work=The New York Times |series=Straight Sets blog |date=15 September 2009 |access-date=18 September 2009 |archive-date=7 October 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111007204147/http://straightsets.blogs.nytimes.com/2009/09/15/can-i-speak-in-spanish/?scp=1&sq=can%20i%20speak%20spanish&st=cse |url-status=live}}</ref> A couple of minutes later, del Potro made the same request again, and only then did Enberg relent saying, "Very quickly, in Spanish, he wants to say hello to his friends here and in Argentina." An emotional del Potro finally spoke a few sentences in Spanish to a cheering crowd. Many viewers expressed disappointment with Enberg and broadcaster [[Tennis on CBS|CBS]] over the interview.<ref name="straightsets"/> A CBS executive later defended Enberg, noting that the contract with the [[United States Tennis Association]] required that certain sponsors receive time during the ceremony.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/09/16/sports/tennis/16enberg.html?ref=sports |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=15 September 2009 |access-date=18 September 2009 |title=CBS Defends Enberg in Trophy Ceremony Backlash |first=Lynn |last=Zinser |archive-date=14 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214040339/http://www.nytimes.com/2009/09/16/sports/tennis/16enberg.html?ref=sports |url-status=live}}</ref> On return to his hometown Tandil, del Potro was greeted by an estimated 40,000 people.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro returns home in triumph |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8260077.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=6 October 2013}}</ref>

In his first match since the US Open, del Potro was upset by world No. 189, [[Édouard Roger-Vasselin]], in straight sets at the [[2009 Rakuten Japan Open Tennis Championships – Singles|Japan Open]] in Tokyo.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.france24.com/en/20091006-roger-vasselin-del-potro-first-round-japan-open-tennis |title=Roger-Vasselin sends del Potro out of Japan Open in first round |publisher=France 24 |date=6 October 2009 |access-date=14 October 2009 |archive-date=15 January 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100115214916/http://www.france24.com/en/20091006-roger-vasselin-del-potro-first-round-japan-open-tennis |url-status=live}}</ref> He then lost his second straight match to Melzer in the second round at the Masters 1000 event in [[2009 Shanghai ATP Masters 1000 – Singles|Shanghai]], retiring while trailing in the second set. At the [[2009 ATP World Tour Finals|ATP World Tour Finals]] in November, he lost his first round-robin match against Andy Murray, but he beat [[Fernando Verdasco]] in his second match to keep his hopes alive. |url=http://www.aamiclassic.com.au/results.php |title=Del Potro wins Kooyong opener |publisher=aamiclassic.com |date=13 January 2010 |access-date=13 January 2010 |url-status=dead 4.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://momento24.com/en/2010/01/11/del-potro-is-now-the-number-4-in-the-world/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120712162135/http://momento24.com/en/2010/01/11/del-potro-is-now-the-number-4-in-the-world/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 July 2012 |title=momento24.com |website=Momento24.com |access-date=11 March 2016}}</ref> He was scheduled to face Jo-Wilfried Tsonga on day 2 of the Kooyong Classic exhibition tournament, but withdrew due to a wrist injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aamiclassic.com.au/news-media.php#story |access-date=30 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110216172807/http://aamiclassic.com.au/news-media.php |archive-date=16 February 2011|title=AAMI Kooyong Classic}}</ref> He came into the [[2010 Australian Open]] with the injury not healed, and took a month off after the event, where he lost in the fourth round to [[Marin Čilić]].<ref name="DP out for a month">{{cite news |title=Del Potro out for at least four weeks |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8511886.stm |url-status=live |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 February 2010 |access-date=28 September 2010 |archive-date=9 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209212123/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8511886.stm}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/tennis/8477424.stm |title=Juan Martin del Potro out of Australian Open |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 January 2010 |access-date=28 September 2010 |archive-date=7 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107080120/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8477424.stm |url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the Australian Open loss, del Potro missed several tournaments, including the [[ATP World Tour Masters 1000|Masters]] tournaments at [[2010 BNP Paribas Open|Indian Wells]] and [[2010 Sony Ericsson Open|Miami]], which were touted as potential return dates,<ref name="DP out for a month"/> due to the persistent wrist injury. Even though he withdrew from the [[2010 Monte-Carlo Rolex Masters|Monte-Carlo Masters]], he regained the world No. 4 ranking, due to Murray's early exit in the second round.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sport.stv.tv/tennis/171198-del-potro-out-since-january-but-overtakes-murray-in-world-rankings/ |title=Del Potro out since January but overtakes Murray |publisher=stv.tv |date=19 April 2010 |access-date=28 September 2010 |archive-date=25 April 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100425040704/http://sport.stv.tv/tennis/171198-del-potro-out-since-january-but-overtakes-murray-in-world-rankings/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> He then withdrew from [[Torneo Godó|Barcelona]] and the [[Rome Masters]]. On 4 May, del Potro took the option of having an operation to fix the injury.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8660453.stm |title=Juan Martin del Potro faces long lay-off after surgery |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 May 2010 |access-date=4 May 2010 |archive-date=7 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107080201/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8660453.stm |url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 May, del Potro said he would not defend his [[US Open (tennis)|US Open]] title, but if all went well, he would appear after the event, targeting the Paris Masters as a possible comeback.<ref>{{cite web |title=Injured Del Potro out of US Open |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8693147.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSTRE64I5DF20100519 |title=Recovering del Potro rules out US Open title |publisher=Reuters |date=19 May 2010 |access-date=19 May 2010 |archive-date=22 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100522173749/http://www.reuters.com/article/idUSTRE64I5DF20100519 |url-status=live}}</ref> However, on 22 July, the USTA stated that del Potro was expected to defend his [[2010 US Open (tennis)|US Open]] crown. Martin del Potro to return a month ahead of schedule | Tennis News |publisher=ESPN |date=23 July 2010 |access-date=11 March 2016 |archive-date=21 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107080111/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/8846577.stm |url-status=live}}</ref> On 2 August, del Potro returned to the practice courts.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://twitpic.com/2b0lcq |title=Que lindo volver a pegarle a la pelotita, aunque fue suave, tuv... on Twitpic |website=Twitpic.com |access-date=11 March 2016 |archive-date=5 August 2010 ===2011: Return to tour, second Davis Cup final===
Del Potro began his 2011 season at the [[2011 Medibank International Sydney|Sydney International]] as a wildcard entry.<ref>{{cite news |title=Del Potro takes Sydney wild card |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2010/12/Other/Sydney-Del-Potro-to-Play.aspx |work=Association of Tennis Professionals |date=8 December 2010 |access-date=1 February 2012 |archive-date=2 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120202143406/http://www.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2010/12/Other/Sydney-Del-Potro-to-Play.aspx |url-status=live}}</ref> In the second round, del Potro was defeated by [[Florian Mayer]] of Germany in straight sets,<ref>{{cite news |title=Juan Martin del Potro loses to Florian Mayer in Sydney |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/9359074.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 January 2011 |access-date=1 February 2012 |archive-date=3 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130903130124/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/9359074.stm |url-status=live}}</ref> despite winning against sixth seed [[Feliciano López]] in three sets in the first round. His next tournament would be the first Grand Slam of the year at the [[2011 Australian Open – Men's singles|2011 Australian Open]], where del Potro was defeated by 21st seed [[Marcos Baghdatis]] in the second round.<ref>{{cite news |title=Baghdatis has little trouble overcoming del Potro |first=Sam |last=Lienert |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/tennis/baghdatis-has-little-trouble-overcoming-del-potro-20110121-19y7w.html |newspaper=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=21 January 2011 |access-date=1 February 2012 |archive-date=25 January 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110125084001/http://www.smh.com.au/sport/australian-open/baghdatis-has-little-trouble-overcoming-del-potro-20110121-19y7w.html |url-status=live}}</ref> As a result, del Potro slipped further down the rankings to No. 485.<ref name="atprankings"/>

After the Australian Open, he participated in the [[2011 SAP Open – Singles|San Jose Open]] where he was accepted into the main draw via a [[Glossary of tennis terms#Protected Ranking|protected ranking]] (PR). He reached the semifinals without dropping a set, however he lost to top seed Fernando Verdasco, in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=San Jose: Verdasco d. Del Potro |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/san-jose-verdasco-d-del-potro |website=Tennis.com |date=13 February 2011}}</ref> Del Potro's next scheduled tournament was the [[2011 Regions Morgan Keegan Championships and the Cellular South Cup|U.S. National Indoor Championships]], where he was accepted into the main draw via a wildcard, losing to top seed and eventual champion [[Andy Roddick]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Roddick downs del Potro, reaches 50th career final |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-roddick-downs-del-potro-reaches-50th-career-final-2011feb19-story.html |website=The San Diego Union-Tribune |date=19 February 2011}}</ref> Del Potro entered the [[Delray Beach International Tennis Championships]] on a wildcard. He defeated [[Ričardas Berankis]], [[Teymuraz Gabashvili]], [[Kevin Anderson (tennis)|Kevin Anderson]] and second-seeded [[Mardy Fish]], to advance to his first ATP final since the 2009 World Tour Finals. In the final, he defeated an erratic Janko Tipsarević in two sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro wins Delray Beach title |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/9409139.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=27 February 2011}}</ref>

Del Potro's next tournament was the ATP Masters at the [[2011 BNP Paribas Open – Men's singles|Indian Wells Masters]]. He reached the semifinals, where he lost to top-seeded [[Rafael Nadal]] in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro advances at Indian Wells |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-del-potro-advances-at-indian-wells-2011mar16-story.html |website=The San Diego Union-Tribune |date=16 March 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Jovica Ilic |title=Indian Wells Flashback: Rafael Nadal beats del Potro to arrange Novak Djokovic clash |url=https://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/Rafael_Nadal/110795/indian-wells-flashback-rafael-nadal-beats-del-potro-to-arrange-novak-djokovic-clash/ |website=Tennis World USA |date=16 March 2022}}</ref> At the [[2011 Sony Ericsson Open|Miami Masters]] he defeated world No. 4, [[Robin Söderling]], in straight sets in round three, before losing to eventual semifinalist [[Mardy Fish]] in straight sets in round four.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro scores first win of year over Top 10 player |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/del-potro-scores-first-win-of-year-over-top-10-player |website=Tennis.com |date=28 March 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Miami: Fish d. Del Potro |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/miami-fish-d-del-potro |website=Tennis.com |date=29 March 2011}}</ref>

In [[2011 Estoril Open|Estoril Open]] del Potro defeated top-seeded [[Robin Söderling]], two time French Open finalist, and dropped just one set in his five matches and took the title against Fernando Verdasco in the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro wins in Estoril |url=https://www.eurosport.com/tennis/del-potro-wins-in-estoril_sto2772966/story.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241217110845/https://www.eurosport.com/tennis/del-potro-wins-in-estoril_sto2772966/story.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 December 2024 |website=Eurosport |date=1 May 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Shrikesh Laxmidas |title=Del Potro overpowers Verdasco to win Estoril Open |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idINIndia-56692020110501 |website=Reuters |date=1 May 2011}}</ref> After suffering an 8-millimeter tear in his left [[rectus abdominis muscle|rectus abdominis]], del Potro withdrew from [[2011 Mutua Madrid Open|Madrid Open]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro withdraws from Madrid with hip injury |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-men-madrid-delpotro-idUSTRE7444ZK20110505 |website=Reuters |date=5 May 2011}}</ref> and did not participate in the [[2011 Internazionali BNL d'Italia|Internazionali BNL d'Italia]], but confirmed that he would play the [[2011 French Open – Men's singles|French Open]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Ed McGrogan |title=Injured del Potro hopes to be fit for Roland Garros |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/injured-del-potro-hopes-to-be-fit-for-roland-garros |website=Tennis.com |date=11 May 2011}}</ref> There he lost in the third round in four sets to second-seeded Novak Djokovic.<ref>{{cite web |title=Novak Djokovic overcomes irritation and Juan Martín del Potro in Paris |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2011/may/28/novak-djokovic-french-open |website=The Guardian |date=29 May 2011}}</ref>

[[File:Juan Martin Del Potro 2011 Wimbledon.jpg|thumb|upright=.7|250px|Del Potro at Wimbledon in 2011]]

Del Potro reached the fourth round at [[2011 Wimbledon Championships|Wimbledon]] for the first time by defeating [[Flavio Cipolla]], [[Olivier Rochus]], and [[Gilles Simon]] but lost in four sets to world No. 1, Rafael Nadal, a match described by The Guardian as the "battle of walking wounded".<ref>{{cite web |author1=Kevin Mitchell |title=Rafael Nadal wins battle of walking wounded with Juan Martín del Potro |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2011/jun/27/rafael-nadal-wimbledon-2011 |website=The Guardian |date=27 June 2011}}</ref> Del Potro returned to the top 20 at world No. 19 for the first time in nearly a year. His next tournament was the [[2011 Farmers Classic – Singles|Los Angeles Open]] in late July, where he received a first-round bye as the second seed. He defeated [[James Blake (tennis)|James Blake]] but lost to [[Ernests Gulbis]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gulbis beats del Potro to semis spot |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2011-07-30/gulbis-topples-del-potro/2817410 |website=ABC News |date=30 July 2011}}</ref>

At the [[2011 Rogers Cup|Canada Masters]], del Potro defeated [[Jarkko Nieminen]] before losing to Marin Čilić in the second round.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro no pudo con el croata Cilic |url=https://www.pagina12.com.ar/diario/deportes/8-174235-2011-08-11.html |website=Página 12 |language=Spanish |date=11 August 2011}}</ref> At the [[2011 Western & Southern Open|Cincinnati Masters]] tournament, del Potro lost to Roger Federer, snapping the two-match winning streak he had against his rival.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Simon Evans |title=Federer sinks Del Potro at Cincinnati Open |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idINIndia-58822820110817 |website=Reuters |date=17 August 2011}}</ref> Del Potro entered the [[2011 US Open (tennis)|2011 US Open]] seeded 18th. He beat [[Filippo Volandri]] and [[Diego Junqueira]] before losing to [[Gilles Simon]] in the third round.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Larry Fine |title=Del Potro's U.S. Open return ends at third hurdle |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-open-delpotro-idUSTRE7840C320110905 |website=Reuters |date=5 September 2011}}</ref>

After the US Open, del Potro played in the [[2011 Davis Cup World Group|Davis Cup]] semifinal against Serbia, winning both of his rubbers against Janko Tipsarević and world No. 1, Novak Djokovic. This helped Argentina to a 3–2 victory over Serbia, booking their place in the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Argentina reach final as tearful Djokovic retires |url=https://www.copadavis.com/en/news/63999.aspx |website=Davis Cup |publisher=International Tennis Federation (ITF) |date=18 September 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Zoran Milosavljevic |title=Argentina reach final after Djokovic retires |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-davis-argentina-idUSTRE78H1EF20110918 |website=Reuters |date=18 September 2011}}</ref> In October he lost in the second round of [[2011 If Stockholm Open|Stockholm Open]] to [[James Blake (tennis)|James Blake]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Blake tops del Potro at Stockholm Open |url=https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2011/10/19/Blake-tops-del-Potro-at-Stockholm-Open/11331319055970/ |website=UPI |date=19 October 2011}}</ref> He then reached the final in [[2011 Erste Bank Open – Singles|Vienna]], losing for the first time to Tsonga.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tsonga beats Del Potro in Vienna final |url=https://www.france24.com/en/20111030-tsonga-beats-del-potro-vienna-final |website=France24 |date=30 October 2011}}</ref> Del Potro then reached the semifinals of the [[2011 Valencia Open 500|Valencia Open 500]], losing to eventual champion [[Marcel Granollers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro's Tour finals bid checked by Granollers |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-men-valencia-idUSTRE7A42GS20111105 |website=Reuters |date=5 November 2011}}</ref> He then withdrew from the [[2011 BNP Paribas Masters|Paris Masters]] due to a shoulder injury, wiping out his chances of qualifying for the [[2011 ATP World Tour Finals|year-end championships]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Ed McGrogan |title=Injured del Potro pulls out of Paris Masters |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/injured-del-potro-pulls-out-of-paris-masters |website=Tennis.com |date=6 November 2011}}</ref>

Del Potro played in the [[2011 Davis Cup World Group|Davis Cup final]] in [[Seville]], losing the second rubber to [[David Ferrer]], despite being two sets to one up, in a match lasting over five hours. With his country down 2–1, del Potro needed to beat [[Rafael Nadal]] in the reverse singles to keep the tie going. Del Potro dominated the first set, but could not keep his level up and lost in four sets.<ref name="2011_guardian_daviscup">{{cite web |title=Rafael Nadal beats Juan Martín del Potro as Spain win Davis Cup |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2011/dec/04/rafael-nadal-spain-davis-cup |website=The Guardian |date=4 December 2011}}</ref> For the third time in six years, Argentina lost in the finals of the Davis Cup World Group, this time 3–1.<ref name="2011_guardian_daviscup"/>

Del Potro finished the year ranked world No. 11, despite being ranked no. 485 at one stage. He was named 2011 ATP Comeback Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Stephen Tignor |title=Can del Potro get a boost from the bronze? |url=https://www.espn.com.au/blog/tennis/post/_/id/22/tennis-juan-martin-del-potro-get-boost-bronze |website=ESPN |date=8 August 2012}}</ref>

===2012: Olympic bronze, back to top 10===

Del Potro's first tournament of the year was the [[2012 Apia International Sydney – Men's singles|Sydney International]], where he was the top seed. He made it to the quarterfinals after receiving a bye into the second round. He defeated [[Łukasz Kubot]] in the second round. In the quarterfinals, he was beaten by [[Marcos Baghdatis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.apiainternational.com.au/scores |title=Scores |date=16 January 2012 |access-date=16 January 2012 |archive-date=10 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110143757/http://www.apiainternational.com.au/scores |url-status=live}}</ref>

In the first round of the [[2012 Australian Open – Men's singles|Australian Open]], del Potro defeated [[Adrian Mannarino]] in four sets.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.australianopen.com/en_AU/news/match_reports/2012-01-16/201201161326693695612.html |title=Del Potro turns tide on Frenchman |date=16 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119012350/http://www.australianopen.com/en_AU/news/match_reports/2012-01-16/201201161326693695612.html |archive-date=19 January 2012}}</ref> He reached the quarterfinals of the Grand Slam for the second time, losing to third-seeded Roger Federer in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Federer destroys Del Potro to reach semis |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2012-01-24/federer-blitzes-del-potro/3790976 |website=ABC News |date=24 January 2012}}</ref>

At [[2012 ABN AMRO World Tennis Tournament|ABN AMRO World Tennis Tournament]] in [[Rotterdam]], he defeated [[Tomáš Berdych]], reaching his first final of an ATP 500 level tournament or higher after returning from his wrist injury in 2010. He lost to Federer in straight sets in the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Roger Federer beats Juan Martin del Potro in Rotterdam final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/17090325 |website=BBC Sport |date=19 February 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Federer downs del Potro to capture second Rotterdam title |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2012/02/19/sport/tennis/tennis-federer-potro-rotterdam/index.html |website=CNN |date=19 February 2012}}</ref> At the Open 13 in Marseille, del Potro defeated Davydenko, Gasquet, Tsonga,<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro bests Tsonga in Marseille |url=https://www.tennis.com.au/news/2012/02/26/del-potro-bests-tsonga-in-marseille |website=Tennis Australia |date=26 February 2012}}</ref> and [[Michaël Llodra]] in the final to win his tenth ATP title.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Eric Salliot |title=Del Potro beats Llodra to win Marseille Open |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-men-marseille-idUSTRE81P0FJ20120226 |website=Reuters |date=26 February 2012}}</ref> At [[2012 Dubai Tennis Championships – Men's singles|Dubai]], he lost in the semis to Federer again in two tiebreaks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dubai: Federer d. Del Potro |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/dubai-federer-d-del-potro |website=Tennis.com |date=2 March 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Erik Gudris |title=Federer escapes from Del Potro in Dubai semis |url=https://www.tennisnow.com/News/Federer-Escapes-From-Del-Potro-in-Dubai-Semis.aspx |website=Tennis Now |date=2 March 2012}}</ref> Del Potro lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2012 BNP Paribas Open|Indian Wells Open]] to Federer for the fourth time that year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rafael Nadal & Roger Federer to meet in Indian Wells semi-final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/17410999 |website=BBC Sport |date=17 March 2012}}</ref> He made it to the fourth round of the [[2012 Sony Ericsson Open – Men's singles|Miami Open]], but lost to David Ferrer in two sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=David Ferrer vs. Juan Martin del Potro {{!}} Miami 2012 |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/scores/match-stats/archive/2012/403/ms009 |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP)}}</ref>

Del Potro started his clay-court campaign of 2012 in the [[2012 Davis Cup World Group|Davis Cup quarterfinals]] against Croatia. He won his first rubber against [[Ivo Karlović]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro draws Argentina level |url=https://www.daviscup.com/en/news/articles/del-potro-draws-argentina-level.aspx |website=Davis Cup |publisher=International Tennis Federation (ITF) |date=6 April 2012}}</ref> and then defeated [[Marin Čilić]] in the reverse singles. At the [[2012 Estoril Open|Estoril Open]], he was the defending champion and the top seed. He did not drop a set en route to the final, where he beat Frenchman [[Richard Gasquet]] in straight sets to collect his 11th ATP title.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro wins Estoril Open |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2012/05/06/sport/tennis/tennis-estoril-munich-blue-clay/index.html |website=CNN |date=6 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro defends crown |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/tennis/story/_/id/7898682/juan-martin-del-potro-wins-2nd-straight-estoril-open |website=ESPN |date=7 May 2012}}</ref> At [[2012 Mutua Madrid Open – Men's singles|Madrid Masters]] he defeated [[Florian Mayer]], [[Mikhail Youzhny]], Marin Čilić and [[Alexandr Dolgopolov]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro into semis |url=https://www.eurosport.com/tennis/madrid-masters/2012/del-potro-into-semis_sto3266929/story.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170520202343/http://www.eurosport.com/tennis/madrid-masters/2012/del-potro-into-semis_sto3266929/story.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=20 May 2017 |website=Eurosport |date=12 May 2012}}</ref> but lost in two tiebreaks to [[Tomáš Berdych]] in the semifinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Madrid: Berdych d. Del Potro |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/madrid-berdych-d-del-potro |website=Tennis.com |date=12 May 2012}}</ref>

At the [[2012 French Open – Men's singles|French Open]], where he was seeded ninth, Del Potro defeated [[Albert Montañés]], [[Édouard Roger-Vasselin]], Marin Čilić and seventh seed Tomáš Berdych before losing to Roger Federer in the quarterfinals in five sets, after being up two sets to love.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/tennis/frenchopen/9312585/French-Open-2012-Roger-Federer-fights-back-from-two-sets-down-against-Juan-Martin-del-Potro-to-reach-semi-finals.html |title=Juan Martín del Potro |access-date=6 June 2012 |location=London |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=5 June 2012 |archive-date=6 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120606151153/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/tennis/frenchopen/9312585/French-Open-2012-Roger-Federer-fights-back-from-two-sets-down-against-Juan-Martin-del-Potro-to-reach-semi-finals.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

At [[2012 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles|Wimbledon]], del Potro beat [[Robin Haase]], [[Go Soeda]], and [[Kei Nishikori]], before losing to David Ferrer in the fourth round.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/jul/03/wimbledon-2012-david-ferrer-del-potro |title=Wimbledon 2012: David Ferrer sees off Juan Martín del Potro |access-date=3 July 2012 |location=London |work=The Guardian |first=Jacob |last=Steinberg |date=3 July 2012 |archive-date=30 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151230162351/http://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/jul/03/wimbledon-2012-david-ferrer-del-potro |url-status=live}}</ref>

Del Potro lost the match, by 17–19 in the third set.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/aug/03/roger-federer-del-potro-olympics?newsfeed=true |work=[[The Guardian]]
