He ended the year ranked world No. 7, with a 65–17 win–loss record and four titles captured throughout the season.<ref name="atp2012">{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro – 2012 player activity |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/players/juan-martin-del-potro/d683/player-activity?year=2012 |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP)}}</ref>

===2013: Wimbledon semifinal, return to top 5===
Del Potro began his season at the [[2013 Australian Open – Men's singles|Australian Open]], where he was upset in the third round by [[Jérémy Chardy]] in five sets. The next month, he won the [[2013 ABN AMRO World Tennis Tournament – Singles|Rotterdam Open]], beating [[Gaël Monfils]], [[Ernest Gulbis]], [[Jarkko Nieminen]], [[Grigor Dimitrov]] in the semifinals, and [[Julien Benneteau]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro rightful winner of anniversary edition |url=http://www.abnamrowtt.com/news-and-media/latest-news/40th-edition/del-potro-rightful-winner-of-anniversary-edition |access-date=17 February 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130220200318/http://www.abnamrowtt.com/news-and-media/latest-news/40th-edition/del-potro-rightful-winner-of-anniversary-edition |archive-date=20 February 2013 |df=dmy}}</ref> At Dubai, del Potro beat [[Marcos Baghdatis]], saving three match points, [[Somdev Devvarman]], and [[Daniel Brands]], but lost in the semifinals to eventual winner Novak Djokovic.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dubai: Djokovic d. Del Potro |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/dubai-djokovic-d-del-potro |website=Tennis.com |date=1 March 2013}}</ref> At Indian Wells in March, del Potro defeated Nikolay Davydenko, [[Björn Phau]], and [[Tommy Haas]]. In the quarterfinals, he beat Andy Murray for the second time in six matches. In the semifinals, he upset top seed and world No. 1 Djokovic, to end the Serb's streak of 22 victories.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro beats Novak Djokovic in Indian Wells semis |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/21818191 |website=BBC Sport |date=17 March 2013}}</ref> He then lost in the final to Rafael Nadal in three sets.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Mark Lamport-Stokes |title=Nadal beats Del Potro to clinch Indian Wells title |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/csports-us-tennis-indian-men-idCABRE92G0L620130317 |website=Reuters |date=18 March 2013}}</ref> Del Potro withdrew from most of the clay-court season and from the [[2013 French Open|French Open]] due to a viral infection.<ref>{{cite web |title=French Open suffers again as Del Potro pulls out |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2013/05/22/sport/tennis/tennis-del-potro-withdraws-from-french-open/index.html |website=CNN |date=23 May 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Del potro Queens 2013.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Del Potro at the Queen's Club, 2013]]
On grass, del Potro began at the [[2013 Aegon Championships – Singles|Queen's Club Championships]], where he won his first comeback match in three sets against [[Xavier Malisse]]. He defeated [[Daniel Evans (tennis)|Daniel Evans]], only to be upset in the quarterfinals by [[Lleyton Hewitt]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Martyn Herman |title=Hewitt rolls back years to beat Del Potro |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-tennis-queens-idUKBRE95D0P120130614 |website=Reuters |date=13 June 2013}}</ref>

At [[2013 Wimbledon Championships|Wimbledon]], Del Potro won against [[Albert Ramos]], [[Jesse Levine]], and [[Grega Žemlja]] before advancing past the fourth round for the first time in his career, thanks to a win over [[Andreas Seppi]]. He then played David Ferrer and, despite slipping badly during the fifth point of the match and aggravating a pre-existing leg injury, requiring over five minutes of treatment and by his own admission being close to forfeiting the match, he recovered to defeat Ferrer in straight sets to advance to his first Grand Slam semifinal since the 2009 US Open without dropping a set. On 5 July, Djokovic defeated him in five sets in 4 hours and 44 minutes, making it at that point the longest semifinal in the history of Wimbledon men's singles.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Ben Dirs |title=Novak Djokovic beats Del Potro to reach Wimbledon final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/23200853 |website=BBC Sport |date=5 July 2013}}</ref>

Del Potro won the [[2013 Citi Open|Washington Open]], beating [[Ryan Harrison (tennis)|Ryan Harrison]], [[Bernard Tomic]], [[Kevin Anderson (tennis)|Kevin Anderson]], Tommy Haas in the semifinals and [[John Isner]] in the final in three sets. Before the final he didn't drop a set. This was his third title at the event and his second of the year.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Taylor Newman |title=Del Potro beats Isner for third title in Washington |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/tennis/2013/08/04/juan-del-potro-john-isner-citi-open/2617281/ |website=USA Today |date=4 August 2013}}</ref> Del Potro reached the semifinals of [[2013 Western & Southern Open – Men's singles|Cincinnati Masters]] where he again faced Isner and lost the match in three sets.<ref>{{cite magazine |author1=Courtney Nguyen |title=John Isner defeats Juan Martin del Potro to make Cincinnati final |url=https://www.si.com/tennis/2013/08/17/top-ranked-american-john-isner-defeats-juan-martin-del-potro-to-make-cincinnati-final |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=17 August 2013}}</ref> Del Potro got to the second round of the [[2013 US Open (tennis)|US Open]], after a four-set victory against [[Guillermo García-López]], only to be upset by Lleyton Hewitt in five sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hewitt stuns Del Potro |url=https://www.eurosport.com/tennis/us-open-5/2013/hewitt-stuns-del-potro_sto3903653/story.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241217142813/https://www.eurosport.com/tennis/us-open-5/2013/hewitt-stuns-del-potro_sto3903653/story.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 December 2024 |website=Eurosport |date=31 August 2013}}</ref>

At the [[2013 Rakuten Japan Open Tennis Championships|Japan Open]], Del Potro, who entered the tournament on a wildcard, beat Marcos Baghdatis, [[Carlos Berlocq]], [[Alexandr Dolgopolov]], [[Nicolas Almagro]] and [[Milos Raonic]] in two sets to win his third title of the year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro wins Japan Open in Tokyo |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/24418482 |website=BBC Sport |date=6 October 2013}}</ref> In October, Del Potro reached the final of the [[2013 Shanghai Rolex Masters|Shanghai Rolex Masters]], defeating [[Philipp Kohlschreiber]], Tommy Haas, Nicolás Almagro, and Rafael Nadal (for the first time since the semifinals of the [[2009 US Open (tennis)|2009 US Open]]) en route, but eventually losing to defending champion Djokovic in a third-set tiebreak.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Jacob Steinberg |title=Novak Djokovic v Juan Martín del Potro: Shanghai Masters final – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2013/oct/13/novak-djokovic-v-juan-martn-del-potro-shanghai-masters-final-live |website=The Guardian |date=13 October 2013}}</ref> In late October he beat sixth-seeded Roger Federer in three sets in the final of the [[2013 Swiss Indoors|Swiss Indoors]], his fourth title of the year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin Del Potro beats Roger Federer in Swiss Indoors final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/24694918 |website=BBC Sport |date=27 October 2013}}</ref> However, he lost to Federer in the quarterfinals of the [[2013 BNP Paribas Masters|Paris Masters]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Roger Federer to meet Novak Djokovic in Paris Masters semi |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/24774761 |website=BBC Sport |date=1 November 2013}}</ref> and in a winner-take-all, round-robin clash in the [[2013 ATP World Tour Finals|ATP World Tour Finals]] at the [[The O2 arena (London)|O<sub>2</sub> arena]] in London.<ref>{{cite web |title=Federer downs del Potro in epic to reach World Tour Finals semis |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2013/11/09/sport/tennis/tennis-federer-del-potro-semis/index.html |website=CNN |date=9 November 2013}}</ref> He finished the year with a 51–16 record, winning four titles overall and prize money of $4,294,039. Del Potro was named Argentina's Sportsman of the Year.<ref name="atp2013">{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro – 2013 player activity |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/players/juan-martin-del-potro/d683/player-activity?year=2012 |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP)}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=News | ATP World Tour | Tennis |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2013/12/50/Del-Potro-Named-Argentina-Sportsman-Of-Year.aspx |publisher=ATP World Tour |access-date=11 March 2016 |archive-date=16 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216105317/http://www.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2013/12/50/Del-Potro-Named-Argentina-Sportsman-Of-Year.aspx |url-status=live}}</ref>

===2014–2015: Second wrist injury, two years away from tour===
Del Potro began his [[2014 ATP World Tour]] season at the [[2014 Apia International Sydney – Men's singles|Sydney International]] as the top seed, winning the final of the tournament against defending champion [[Bernard Tomic]] in only 53 minutes.<ref name="Sydney14">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/tennis/25696901 |title=Juan Martin del Potro beats Bernard Tomic in Sydney final |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=11 January 2014 |access-date=11 March 2016 |archive-date=24 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924233205/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/tennis/25696901 |url-status=live}}</ref> It was his fifth title as top seed.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2014/01/2/Sydney-Saturday-del-Potro-Tomic.aspx |title=News | ATP World Tour | Tennis |publisher=ATP World Tour |access-date=11 March 2016 |archive-date=11 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111211819/http://www.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2014/01/2/Sydney-Saturday-del-Potro-Tomic.aspx |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Juan Martin del Potro Dubai 2014.jpg|thumb|250px|Del Potro at the [[2014 Dubai Tennis Championships – Men's singles|2014 Dubai Tennis Championships]]]]
When asked to play for Argentina in the Davis Cup, del Potro declined, arguing problems with the press and the team, and his decision to prioritize his personal career.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cronica.com.ar/diario/2013/11/15/59710-otra-vez-del-potro-se-bajo-de-la-davis-2014.html |access-date=3 February 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221173744/http://www.cronica.com.ar/diario/2013/11/15/59710-otra-vez-del-potro-se-bajo-de-la-davis-2014.html |archive-date=21 February 2014 |title=Otra vez: Del Potro se bajó de la Davis 2014|language=es}}</ref>

At the [[2014 Australian Open – Men's singles|Australian Open]], he won his opening match against [[Rhyne Williams]], but lost to [[Roberto Bautista-Agut]] in the second round, having led two sets to one. Despite his second-round loss, del Potro returned to being world No. 4. After the Australian Open, del Potro required treatment for his left wrist, which had been giving him trouble since 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tennis.si.com/2014/01/28/juan-martin-del-potro-left-wrist-injury/ |title=Juan Martin del Potro receiving treatment for wrist injury |website=Sports Illustrated |date=2014-01-28 |access-date=2016-03-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140406184906/http://tennis.si.com/2014/01/28/juan-martin-del-potro-left-wrist-injury/ |archive-date=6 April 2014 |df=dmy-all}}</ref>

In February, at the [[2014 ABN AMRO World Tennis Tournament|2014 Rotterdam Open]], he eased past [[Gaël Monfils]] and [[Paul-Henri Mathieu]] in straight sets, but fell to Latvian [[Ernests Gulbis]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gulbis upsets del Potro, Cilic beats Murray in Rotterdam |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/gulbis-upsets-del-potro-cilic-beats-murray-in-rotterdam |website=Tennis.com |date=14 February 2014}}</ref> In the [[2014 Dubai Tennis Championships]], he retired against [[Somdev Devvarman]] after losing the first set due to his wrist injury and said "It was really tough to play today. I tried everything. I cannot be the player I would like to be."<ref>{{cite web |title=Djokovic wins, Del Potro retires in Dubai |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/tennis/2014/02/25/djokovic-wins-del-potro-retires-in-dubai/5803493/ |website=USA Today |date=25 February 2014}}</ref> The same injury led to his subsequent withdrawal from Masters 1000 series events in [[2014 BNP Paribas Open|Indian Wells]] and [[2014 Sony Open Tennis|Miami]], meaning that del Potro dropped to world No. 8.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Kamakshi Tandon |title=Del Potro withdraws from Indian Wells, will try to play Miami |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/del-potro-withdraws-from-indian-wells-will-try-to-play-miami |website=Tennis.com |date=9 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro withdraws from Miami with wrist injury |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-tennis-del-potro-idUKBREA2J02S20140320 |website=Reuters |date=20 March 2014}}</ref>

Del Potro underwent surgery in March 2014 to repair the problem in his left wrist, missing the rest of the 2014 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Juan Martin del Potro to miss the rest of the season? |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2014/03/24/sport/tennis/juan-martin-del-potro-injury-tennis/index.html |publisher=CNN |date=24 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Courtney Nguyen |title=Photo: Juan Martin del Potro gives thumbs up after wrist surgery |url=https://www.si.com/tennis/2014/03/24/photo-juan-martin-del-potro-wrist-surgery |website=SI |date=24 March 2014}}</ref>

Del Potro began his [[2015 ATP World Tour|2015]] season with wrist pain and was not sure whether he would play Sydney and the [[2015 Australian Open]]. However, at the last minute he decided to play both tournaments.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://uk.mobile.reuters.com/article/idUKL3N0UM3DX20150107?irpc=932 |title=Tennis-Del Potro to play in Sydney despite wrist worries |agency=Reuters |date=7 January 2015 |access-date=2016-03-11 |archive-date=7 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107080125/https://www.reuters.com/article/idUKL3N0UM3DX20150107?edition-redirect=uk |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Christopher Clarey |author2=Gardiner Harris |title=Juan Martín del Potro decides wrist isn't ready for Australian Open |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/01/18/sports/tennis/Juan-Martn-del-Potro-Decides-Wrist-Isnt-Ready-for-Australian-Open.html |website=The New York Times |date=17 January 2015}}</ref> He had not played a tournament since February 2014, but he started the [[2015 Apia International Sydney – Men's singles|Sydney International]] with a straight-sets win against [[Sergiy Stakhovsky]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martín del Potro makes winning return at Sydney International |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/jan/13/juan-martin-del-potro-winning-return-sydney-international |website=The Guardian |date=13 January 2015}}</ref> In the second round he defeated world No. 19 and top seed [[Fabio Fognini]] to reach the quarterfinals, which he lost to [[Mikhail Kukushkin]] in two tiebreakers.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sydney International Juan Martin del Potro knocked out by Mikhail Kukushkin in quarter-finals |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-01-15/del-potro-knocked-out-of-sydney-international-by-kukushkin/6019768 |agency=ABC |date=15 January 2015}}</ref> Del Potro withdrew from the [[2015 Australian Open]], due to his wrist injury, the day before his first match and had another surgery on his left wrist.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://m.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2015/01/2/Australian-Open-Del-Potro-Withdraws.aspx |title=Official Site of Men's Professional Tennis | ATP World Tour | Tennis |website=M.atpworldtour.com |access-date=2016-03-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150203203644/http://m.atpworldtour.com/News/Tennis/2015/01/2/Australian-Open-Del-Potro-Withdraws.aspx |archive-date=3 February 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro undergoes more surgery on left wrist |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/30921383 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro has another operation on left wrist |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-men-delpotro-idUSKBN0KU15120150121 |website=Reuters |date=21 January 2015}}</ref> In late March Del Potro played in the [[2015 Miami Open – Men's singles|Miami Open]] with a protected ranking and lost his first-round match to [[Vasek Pospisil]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro loses first-round match at Miami Open |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/tennis/2015/03/26/del-potro-loses-1st-round-match-at-miami-open/70497524/ |website=USA Today |date=26 March 2015}}</ref> It would be his last match of the year, undergoing wrist surgery again in June 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/35488983 |title=Juan Martin del Potro to make return at Delray Beach |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2016-02-03 |access-date=2016-03-11 |archive-date=20 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620042809/https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/35488983 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===2016: Comeback, Olympic silver, Davis Cup champion===
He played his first tournament since undergoing surgery at the [[2016 Delray Beach International Tennis Championships|Delray Beach Open]] in mid February.<ref name="delray2016">{{cite web |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-comeback-delray-beach-2016 |title=Del Potro Returns To Action In Delray Beach |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date= 3 February 2016 |archive-date=6 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160206011210/http://www.atpworldtour.com/en/news/del-potro-comeback-delray-beach-2016 |url-status=live}}</ref> In his first competitive match in almost a year, del Potro defeated [[Denis Kudla]] in two sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro wins in return, beats Kudla at Delray Beach Open |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/tennis/2016/02/16/top-seeded-kevin-anderson-quits-delray-beach-open/80464514/ |website=USA Today |date=16 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro makes winning return |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-kudla-delray-beach-2016-tuesday |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=17 February 2016}}</ref> He followed this up with a straight sets win over Australian [[John-Patrick Smith]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro gets it done |url=https://yellowtennisball.com/del-potro-gets-it-done/ |website=Delray Beach Open |date=18 February 2016 |access-date=31 August 2023 |archive-date=31 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230831195426/https://yellowtennisball.com/del-potro-gets-it-done/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He defeated [[Jérémy Chardy]] in two sets in the quarterfinal, reaching his first semifinal since 2014; which he lost to eventual champion [[Sam Querrey]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Querrey snuffs out Del Potro's hopes of fairytale return |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-delray-delpotro-idUSKCN0VU040 |website=Reuters |date=20 February 2016}}</ref> At [[Indian Wells Masters|Indian Wells]], he beat [[Tim Smyczek]] in two sets. He lost in the next round to [[Tomas Berdych]] in straight sets. At [[Miami Open (tennis)|Miami Open]] he beat [[Guido Pella]] in two sets and was set to play Roger Federer for the first time in more than two years, but just hours before the match Federer withdrew due to a stomach virus.<ref>{{cite web |title=Roger Federer misses Miami Open because of stomach virus |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/mar/25/roger-federer-miami-open-juan-martin-del-potro |website=The Guardian |date=5 March 2016}}</ref> Instead he played lucky loser and countryman [[Horacio Zeballos]] and lost in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lucky Zeballos Downs Del Potro In Miami |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/zeballos-beats-del-potro-in-miami-2016 |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=25 March 2016}}</ref>

Del Potro then competed in his first clay-court tournament since 2013 at the [[2016 BMW Open|BMW Open]] in Munich in late April. He beat [[Dustin Brown (tennis)|Dustin Brown]], in two sets and [[Jan-Lennard Struff]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin Del Potro reaches Munich Open quarter-final |url=https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/12110/10261667/juan-martin-del-potro-reaches-munich-open-quarter-final |website=Sky Sports |date=28 April 2016}}</ref> in his first three-set match of the year but lost to Philipp Kohlschreiber in the quarterfinals in straight sets. At [[2016 Mutua Madrid Open|Madrid Open]] he had his best victory after coming back on the tour, defeating 14th seed [[Dominic Thiem]] in straight sets but lost his next match to [[Jack Sock]] in two sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro fue eliminado en 2da ronda en Madrid |url=https://www.diariojornada.com.ar/158875/deportes/del_potro_fue_eliminado_en_2da_ronda_en_madrid |website=Diario Jornada |language=Spanish |date=4 May 2016}}</ref> At [[2016 MercedesCup|Stuttgart Open]], his first grass tournament since the [[2013 Wimbledon Championships]], he beat Grigor Dimitrov in straight sets, [[John Millman]] in two sets and [[Gilles Simon]] in three sets, before losing to Kohlschreiber in straight sets in the semis.<ref name="ms2016stuttgart">{{cite web|title=2016 Stuttgart Outdoor – Singles draw|url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/en/scores/archive/stuttgart/321/2016/draws?matchType=singles|publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP)}}</ref>

[[File:Juan Martín del Potro - Rio 2016.jpg|thumb|200px|Del Potro at the [[2016 Summer Olympics]]]]
At [[2016 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles|Wimbledon]] he beat [[Stephane Robert]] and [[Stanislas Wawrinka]] (in four sets).<ref>{{cite web |author1=Simon Cambers |title=Juan Martín del Potro rallies to sink Stan Wawrinka at Wimbledon |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/jul/01/juan-martin-del-potro-stan-wawrinka-wimbledon |website=The Guardian |date=1 July 2016}}</ref> Del Potro then lost in an ill-tempered four-set match against 32nd seed [[Lucas Pouille]] in the third round.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Bryan Armen Graham |title=Juan Martín del Potro's revival threatened by 'shut up' row with Pouille |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/jul/02/wimbledon-del-potro-pouille-mens-singles |website=The Guardian |date=2 July 2016}}</ref>

In the [[Tennis at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|2016 Olympic Games]], held at the [[Olympic Tennis Centre (Rio de Janeiro)|Olympic Tennis Centre]] in Rio de Janeiro, del Potro defeated top seed and world No. 1, Novak Djokovic, in the first round, winning two tiebreaks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rio Olympics 2016: Novak Djokovic beaten by Juan Martin del Potro in first round |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/37007510 |website=BBC Sport |date=8 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Bryan Armen Graham |title=Novak Djokovic in tears after shock Olympic defeat by Juan Martín del Potro |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/aug/07/novak-djokovic-rio-2016-juan-martin-del-potro |website=The Guardian |date=8 August 2016}}</ref> It was a significant win for him because he was ranked no. 145 in the world and was coming back from an injury. He also defeated [[João Sousa]], [[Taro Daniel]] in three sets and top-20 player Bautista Agut to guarantee a medal match. He played 2008 gold medalist and the 2016 doubles gold medalist, Rafael Nadal. He defeated him in three tight sets to guarantee a medal. Del Potro played in his first gold medal match against the reigning Wimbledon champion from the previous month, Andy Murray and lost in four grueling sets in over four hours.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Michael Rosenberg |title=Juan Martin del Potro found game, Olympic spirit in road to silver medal in tennis |url=https://www.si.com/olympics/2016/08/15/juan-martin-del-potro-tennis-silver-medal-rio-olympics |website=SI |date=14 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Gustavo Goitia |title=Juan Martin del Potro and the stuff of dreams |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/summer/tennis/story/_/id/17310838/juan-martin-del-potro-stuff-dreams |website=ESPN |date=15 August 2016}}</ref> However, del Potro said after beating Nadal "I already won silver, that's good enough for me."

At the [[2016 US Open – Men's singles|US Open]] Del Potro's ranking of No. 141 was not sufficient to gain direct entry into the main draw but he was granted a wild card.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Ben Rothenberg |author2=Christopher Clarey |title=Argentina's Juan Martín del Potro Receives Wild Card Into U.S. Open |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/08/17/sports/tennis/juan-martin-del-potro-to-receive-wild-card-into-us-open.html |website=The New York Times |date=16 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin Del Potro given US Open wild card after Olympics final loss |url=https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/12110/10539217/juan-martin-del-potro-given-us-open-wild-card-after-olympics-final-loss |website=Sky Sports |author=Andrew Dickson |date=16 August 2016}}</ref> He beat countryman [[Diego Schwartzman]] in straight sets, 19th seed and top-ranked American [[Steve Johnson (tennis)|Steve Johnson]] in straight sets,<ref>{{cite web |author1=Toby Keel |title=Juan Martín del Potro looked somwhere close to his very best in ousting Steve Johnson |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/tennis/us-open-men/2016/juan-martin-del-potro-v-steve-johnson-live_sto5815915/story.shtml |website=[[TNT Sports]] |date=2 September 2016}}</ref> 11th seed and Grand Slam finalist David Ferrer in straight sets and eighth seed Dominic Thiem (when Thiem retired during the second set). Del Potro then lost to eventual champion Stan Wawrinka in the quarterfinals in four sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=No more tears: Stan Wawrinka ends Juan Martin del Potro's U.S. Open run |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/no-more-tears-stan-wawrinka-ends-juan-martin-del-potro-s-u-s-open-run |website=Tennis.com |date=8 September 2016}}</ref>

Del Potro then played against Murray, in a rematch of the Olympic final, in the [[2016 Davis Cup World Group|Davis Cup]] semifinal, held in [[Glasgow]]. Del Potro won the thrilling five-set match in 5 hours and 7 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Kevin Mitchell |title=Juan Martín del Potro takes revenge for Olympics on Andy Murray in Davis Cup |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/sep/16/andy-murray-davis-cup-juan-martin-del-potro-tennis-match-report |website=The Guardian |date=16 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Davis Cup: Juan Martin del Potro beats Andy Murray, Guido Pella beats Kyle Edmund |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/37386673 |website=BBC Sport |date=16 September 2016}}</ref> Del Potro was granted a wildcard for the [[2016 Shanghai Rolex Masters|Shanghai Masters]] in October, where he lost in the first round in three sets to 11th seed [[David Goffin]], despite being a set and a break up.<ref>{{cite web |title=Goffin sends Del Potro crashing out of Shanghai Masters |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/sports/1107921/goffin-sends-del-potro-crashing-out-of-shanghai-masters |website=Bangkok Post |date=11 October 2016}}</ref> Del Potro was given a wild card into the [[Stockholm Open]] and beat John Isner, Nicolas Almagro, [[Ivo Karlovic]], Grigor Dimitrov and Jack Sock to win his first title since his return from injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro wins Stockholm Open for first ATP title since 2014 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/37751747 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 October 2016}}</ref> Del Potro then played at the [[2016 Swiss Indoors|Swiss Indoors]], where he comfortably beat qualifier [[Robin Haase]] in the first round. He then got revenge on Goffin in a straight sets win, before falling in two tight sets to [[Kei Nishikori]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nishikori ousts Del Potro in Swiss Indoors quarterfinals |url=https://apnews.com/article/3b441c4e9ad44ef0a211e9be064842f8 |website=AP |date=28 October 2016}}</ref>

Vying for Argentina's first title, del Potro played in the [[2016 Davis Cup]] against Croatia. His first match was a four set victory against Ivo Karlović. Partnering [[Leonardo Mayer]], del Potro lost in doubles against [[Ivan Dodig]] and Marin Čilić. 2–1 down in matches, del Potro played in singles against Čilić, coming back from two sets down for the first time in his career to win in five sets. Described as one of the best Davis Cup comebacks ever, del Potro levelled the score at 2–2, paving the way for [[Federico Delbonis]] to complete the comeback by beating Ivo Karlović, in straight sets, thus claiming Argentina's first ever Davis Cup title.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/11/27/sports/tennis/argentina-rallies-against-croatia-to-win-first-davis-cup-title.html |title=Argentina Rallies Against Croatia to Win First Davis Cup Title |newspaper=The New York Times |date=27 November 2016 |access-date=25 February 2017 |archive-date=12 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170112120124/https://www.nytimes.com/2016/11/27/sports/tennis/argentina-rallies-against-croatia-to-win-first-davis-cup-title.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martín del Potro inspires Argentina to first Davis Cup title in Croatia |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/nov/27/juan-martin-del-potro-argentina-davis-cup-title-croatia |website=The Guardian |date=27 November 2016}}</ref>

For the second time in his career, after 2011, del Potro was named ATP Comeback Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro Honoured As 2016 Comeback Player Of The Year |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-honoured-as-comeback-player-of-the-year-atp-awards-2016 |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

===2017: 20th title, US Open semifinal===
Del Potro decided to skip the [[2017 Australian Open]] and made his season debut at the [[2017 Delray Beach International Tennis Championships|Delray Beach Open]], where he was seeded in a tournament for the first time in three years, at No. 7, and won his first three matches against [[Kevin Anderson (tennis)|Kevin Anderson]], [[Damir Dzumhur]] and [[Sam Querrey]]. However, in the semifinals, del Potro lost to top seed and world No. 4 [[Milos Raonic]] in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raonic Fights Through Del Potro In Delray Beach |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/raonic-sock-delray-beach-2017-saturday/ |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=26 February 2017}}</ref> Next, del Potro played in the [[2017 Abierto Mexicano Telcel|Mexican Open]], where he was drawn to play qualifier [[Frances Tiafoe]], who idolised del Potro when he was a child. Del Potro won in a tight three-set match.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Lorenzo Ciotti |title=Frances Tiafoe: "Juan Martin Del Potro is my hero" |url=https://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/Tennis_Interviews/129250/frances-tiafoe-juan-martin-del-potro-is-my-hero-/ |website=Tennis World |date=2 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro and Tiafoe have a spectacular opening debut in Acapulco |url=https://abiertomexicanodetenis.com/en/2017/03/01/del-potro-and-tiafoe-have-a-spectacular-opening-debut-in-acapulco/ |website=Abierto Mexicano de Tennis |date=1 March 2017}}</ref> In the next round, del Potro lost in three sets to Djokovic after winning the first set.<ref>{{cite web |title=Novak Djokovic turns back Juan Martin del Potro in Mexico |url=https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/18801092/novak-djokovic-thwarts-juan-martin-del-potro-reach-mexico-quarterfinals |website=ESPN |date=1 March 2017}}</ref>

At the [[2017 BNP Paribas Open|Indian Wells Masters]] he beat his Argentine [[Davis Cup]] teammate [[Federico Delbonis]] in two tight sets before losing to Djokovic in three sets.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Andrew L. John |title=Novak Djokovic grabs historic win at Indian Wells |url=https://eu.desertsun.com/story/sports/tennis/bnp/2017/03/15/novak-djokovic-grabs-historic-win-indian-wells/99197984/ |website=The Federer eases past Juan Martin del Potro in Miami |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/tennis/miami-masters/2017/roger-federer-eases-past-juan-martin-del-potro-in-miami_sto6109341/story.shtml |website=[[TNT Sports]] |date=28 March 2017}}</ref> Del Potro began his clay-court season at the [[2017 Estoril Open|Estoril Open]], where he beat [[Yuichi Sugita]] for the loss of just four games in |url=http://www.eurosport.co.uk/tennis/juan-martin-del-potro-withdraws-from-estoril-open-following-grandfathers-death_sto6151875/story.shtml |title=Juan Martin del Potro withdraws from Estoril Open |url-status=live}}</ref> Del Potro withdrew from the [[2017 Mutua Madrid Open|Madrid Open]], reappearing at the [[2017 Internazionali BNL d'Italia|Italian Open]] where he reached the quarterfinals of a Masters 1000 tournament for the first time since the [[2013 BNP Paribas Masters|2013 Paris Masters]], following victories over 10th seed Grigor Dimitrov,<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro Stays Perfect Against Dimitrov |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-dimitrov-rome-2017-monday |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=15 May 2017}}</ref> [[Kyle Edmund]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro overcomes Kyle Edmund in Rome |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/tennis/rome-masters/2017/juan-martin-del-potro-overcomes-kyle-edmund-in-rome_sto6169445/story.shtml |website=[[TNT Sports]] |date=18 May 2017}}</ref> and seventh seed [[Kei Nishikori]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro knocks Nishikori out of Italian Open |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2017/05/19/tennis/del-potro-knocks-nishikori-italian-open/ |website=The [[File:JMDP Lyon 2017.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Del Potro at the [[2017 Lyon Open]]]]

In May at [[2017 Lyon Open|Lyon Open]], del Potro defeated lucky loser [[Quentin Halys]], but lost in the next round against Portuguese qualifier [[Gastão Elias]] in straight sets. Doubt was cast over his participation at the [[2017 French Open – Men's singles|French Open]] because of a back injury that had hampered him at Lyon, but he eventually decided to partake in the event.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro could miss French Open because of injuries |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/juan-martin-del-potro-could-miss-french-open-because-of-injuries |website=Tennis.com |date=24 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro sails through on French Open return after injury scare |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/csports-us-tennis-frenchopen-delpotro-idCAKBN18Q15W-OCASP |website=Reuters |date=30 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro's act of sportsmanship at French Open earns plaudits |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2017/06/01/tennis/french-open-tennis-del-potro-murray/index.html |website=CNN |date=1 June 2017}}</ref> Del Potro entered the event after a five-year absence as the 29th seed, the first time since the [[2014 Australian Open]] that he was seeded at a Grand Slam tournament. In the first round he defeated [[Guido Pella]] in straight sets,<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro sails through on French Open return after injury scare |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-frenchopen-delpotro-idUSKBN18Q15W |website=Reuters |date=30 May 2017}}</ref> and in the second round against Nicolás Almagro, it was one set apiece before Almagro retired. Del Potro eventually fell in straight sets to top seed Andy Murray in the third round.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/en/news/roland-garros-2017-saturday1-murray-del-potro-isner|title=Murray Takes Titanic Tussle To Reach Fourth Round {{!}} ATP World Tour {{!}} Tennis|work=ATP World Tour|access-date=2017-06-17|language=en|archive-date=7 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170607091259/http://www.atpworldtour.com/en/news/roland-garros-2017-saturday1-murray-del-potro-isner|url-status=live}}</ref>

After suffering a second round exit at Wimbledon in straight sets against [[Ernests Gulbis]],<ref>{{cite web |author1=Simon Cambers |author2=Jacob Steinberg |title=World No589 Gulbis returns from wilderness to shock Del Potro |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/jul/06/kyle-edmund-gael-monfils-centre-court-wimbledon-2017 |website=The Guardian |date=6 July 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Mark Hodgkinson |title=Gulbis dispatches Del Potro to book date with Djokovic |url=https://www.wimbledon.com/en_GB/news/articles/2017-07-06/gulbis_dispatches_del_potro_to_book_date_with_djokovic.html |website=Wimbledon |publisher=AELTC |date=6 July 2017}}</ref> Del Potro began his summer North American hardcourt season in [[2017 Citi Open – Men's singles|Washington]], where he lost to Kei Nishikori in the third round, ending his 15-match winning streak at the event.<ref>{{cite web |title=Flashback: Del Potro's Washington Hat Trick |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-washington-three-titles |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=6 August 2020}}</ref> He then lost in two sets to [[Denis Shapovalov]] in the second round at the [[2017 Rogers Cup – Men's singles|Canadian Open]] in Montreal,<ref>{{cite web |title=Shapovalov Beats del Potro To Delight Montreal Crowd |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/shapovalov-del-potro-montreal-2017-wednesday |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=9 August 2017}}</ref> and at the [[2017 Western & Southern Open – Men's singles|Cincinnati Masters]] he won against [[Tomáš Berdych]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro makes winning return to Cincinnati |url=https://www.marca.com/en/more-sports/2017/08/16/59940ca022601d7b228b4607.html |website=Marca |date=16 August 2017}}</ref> in the first round and qualifier [[Mitchell Krueger]] in the second before losing to eventual champion Grigor Dimitrov in the third round.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dimitrov beats Del Potro for first time to reach Cincinnati quarters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-tennis-cincinnati-men-idUKKCN1AX2R5 |website=Reuters |date=17 August 2017}}</ref>

At the US Open, Del Potro defeated [[Henri Laaksonen]], [[Adrián Menéndez-Maceiras]] and Roberto Bautista Agut in straight sets. He began his fourth round match against Dominic Thiem struggling, falling two sets behind. However, he then raised his level and, with the help of the crowd, eventually prevailed in five sets, saving two match points in the fourth set with two aces. In the post match interview he admitted he considered retiring from the match during the second set.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/del-potro-almost-retired-during-050927734.html |title=Tennis: Del Potro almost retired during epic Thiem win at US Open |date=5 September 2017 |access-date=9 September 2017 |archive-date=9 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909143450/https://sports.yahoo.com/del-potro-almost-retired-during-050927734.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

The US Open account on Instagram switched his racquet for Thor's hammer using software editing tools,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/buzz/2017/09/05/59ae391022601d292f8b461f.html|title=US Open: Federer rebautiza a del Potro como "Juan Martin del THORtro"|date=5 September 2017|access-date=9 September 2017|archive-date=9 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909143306/http://www.marca.com/buzz/2017/09/05/59ae391022601d292f8b461f.html |url-status=live}}</ref> which created a new nickname for the Argentine: Juan Martin "del Thortro", by fellow tennis player [[Roger Federer]], adding to a collection of nicknames such as "Delpo", "Tower of Tandil", "Palito" (stick) and "Enano" (midget).<ref>{{cite web |title=5 Things About U.S. Open Winner Juan Martin del Potro |url=http://people.com/celebrity/5-things-about-u-s-open-winner-juan-martin-del-potro/ |access-date=9 September 2017 |archive-date=9 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909142546/http://people.com/celebrity/5-things-about-u-s-open-winner-juan-martin-del-potro/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In the quarterfinals he defeated Roger Federer in four tight sets; his second victory over the Swiss at the US Open, having beaten him in the final in 2009.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Kevin Mitchell |title=Mighty Juan Martín del Potro scuppers hopes of Federer-Nadal clash at US Open |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/sep/07/mighty-juan-martin-del-potro-scuppers-hopes-of-federer-nadal-clash-at-us-open |website=The Guardian |date=7 September 2017}}</ref> By doing so he reached his first major semifinal since Wimbledon 2013. His run came to an end in four sets, losing to world No. 1, Rafael Nadal.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Kevin Mitchell |title=Rafael Nadal silences Juan Martín del Potro to surge into US Open final |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/sep/08/rafael-nadal-juan-martin-del-potro-report |website=The Guardian |date=9 September 2017}}</ref>

Del Potro began his Asian hard court swing in [[2017 China Open (tennis)|Beijing]], where he lost in straight sets to Grigor Dimitrov in the second round, his second loss against the Bulgarian.<ref>{{cite web |title=Grigor Dimitrov dumps Juan Martin del Potro to reach China Open last eight, Nick Kyrgios impresses |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/tennis/atp-beijing/2017/grigor-dimitrov-dumps-juan-martin-del-potro-to-reach-china-open-last-eight-nick-kyrgios-impresses_sto6355651/story.shtml |website=[[TNT Sports]] |date=5 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Dimitrov Sweeps delPo, Into Beijing QFs |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/dimitrov-del-potro-beijing-2017-wednesday |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=4 October 2017}}</ref> This was followed by the [[2017 Shanghai Rolex Masters – Singles|Shanghai Masters]], where he reached the semifinals of a Masters 1000 event for the first time since 2013 (also in Shanghai), most notably upsetting [[Alexander Zverev Jr.|Alexander Zverev]] in the third round, his second triumph over a Top 5 ranked opponent after his victory over Roger Federer at the [[2017 US Open – Men's singles|US Open]]. Del Potro won the first set but eventually lost in the semifinals against Federer, who would go on to win the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |title=Roger Federer edges past Juan Martin del Potro to set up Shanghai Masters final against Rafael Nadal |url=https://metro.co.uk/2017/10/14/roger-federer-edges-past-juan-martin-del-potro-to-set-up-shanghai-masters-final-against-rafael-nadal-7000171/ |website=Metro |date=14 October 2017}}</ref>

Del Potro defended his 2016 Stockholm Open title by defeating Grigor Dimitrov in the finals of the 2017 Stockholm Open in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stockholm Open: Juan Martin Del Potro beats Grigor Dimitrov in final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/41715511 |website=BBC Sport |date=22 October 2017}}</ref> This victory gave Del Potro his 20th ATP career title. He then reached the final of [[2017 Swiss Indoors – Singles|Basel]], where he faced Federer and again lost in three sets after winning the first.<ref>{{cite web |title=Swiss Indoors: Roger Federer beats Juan Martin del Potro to win eighth Basel title |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/41796315 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 October 2017}}</ref> Del Potro then made it to the quarterfinals of the [[2017 Rolex Paris Masters – Singles|Paris Masters]], where he was one win away from entering the top 10 and qualifying for the [[2017 ATP Finals – Singles|ATP Finals]], which would have been his first time since 2013 participating in the year-end tournament. However, he was defeated in three sets by [[John Isner]] and subsequently declined to be chosen as an alternate for the tournament, instead choosing to rest with his family and friends in his native [[Tandil]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Pete Sharland |title=Juan Martin del Potro falls short in bid for London with John Isner defeat |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/tennis/paris-masters/2017/juan-martin-del-potro-falls-short-in-bid-for-london-with-john-isner-defeat_sto6397156/story.shtml |website=[[TNT Sports]] |date=3 November 2017}}</ref> Nevertheless, Del Potro won 730 points in a span of three weeks and reached the 11th spot of the [[ATP rankings]].

===2018: First Masters, second US Open final, world No. 3, injuries===
{{Main|2018 Juan Martín del Potro tennis season}}
Del Potro started the season at the [[2018 ASB Classic|ASB Classic]] in New Zealand, where he beat Denis Shapovalov to return to the top 10 of the ATP rankings for the first time since August 2014.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Jonathon Braden |title=He's Back In The Top 10, But Does Del Potro Feel Like He's Back? |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-delray-beach-2018-feature |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=20 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=David Long |title=Roberto Bautista Agut defeats Juan Martin del Potro in ASB Classic final |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/tennis/100555445/roberto-bautista-agut-defeats-juan-martin-del-potro-in-asb-classic-final |website=Stuff |date=13 January 2018}}</ref> Del Potro then defeated [[Karen Khachanov]] and David Ferrer en route to the final, where he lost to Roberto Bautista Agut in three sets.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Michael Burgess |author2=Liam Napier |title=Tennis: Juan Martin del Potro storms into ASB Classic semi final |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/tennis/tennis-juan-martin-del-potro-storms-into-asb-classic-semi-final/S7WJQGRIPNTWTKKFNFHSQEABJY/ |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=11 January 2018}}</ref>
At the [[2018 Australian Open|Australian Open]] he lost in the third round against [[Tomáš Berdych]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Berdych topples Del Potro to reach fourth round |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-berdych-australian-open-2018-saturday |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=20 January 2018}}</ref> At the [[2018 Delray Beach Open – Singles|Delray Beach Open]] he was seeded second but lost in the second round to eventual champion [[Frances Tiafoe]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Michael Graham |title=Brilliant Frances Tiafoe upsets Juan Martin del Potro at Delray Beach |url=https://www.tennis365.com/atp-tour/brilliant-frances-tiafoe-upsets-juan-martin-del-potro-delray-beach |website=Tennis365 |date=23 February 2018}}</ref> He then won the [[Acapulco Open]], defeating [[Kevin Anderson (tennis)|Kevin Anderson]] in straight sets to obtain his 21st title, and his biggest title since [[2013 Swiss Indoors]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Delpo hoists biggest trophy in years |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-anderson-acapulco-2018-final |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=3 March 2018}}</ref>

[[File:Del Potro en Indian Wells 2018.jpg|thumb|200px|Del Potro at the [[2018 BNP Paribas Open]], where he won his first Masters 1000 title of his career]]
His winning streak would not stop there, however, as he went on to win the [[2018 BNP Paribas Open|Indian Wells Open]], the first [[ATP Tour Masters 1000|Masters 1000]] tournament of his career, beating teenager [[Alex De Minaur]], veteran David Ferrer, compatriot [[Leonardo Mayer]],  Philipp Kohlschreiber, Milos Raonic and reigning champion and world No. 1, Roger Federer in the final. Del Potro prevailed in three sets despite Federer serving for the match in the decider and holding three championship points.<ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Wells men's final: Juan Martin del Potro beats Roger Federer – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2018/mar/18/roger-federer-juan-martin-del-potro-indian-wells-mens-final-latest-score |website=The Guardian |date=18 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Christopher Clarey |title=Juan Martín del Potro Outlasts Roger Federer for Indian Wells Title |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/18/sports/tennis/del-potro-federer-indian-wells.html |website=The New York Times |date=18 March 2018}}</ref> This was del Potro's biggest achievement in the ATP Tour after the [[2009 US Open (tennis)|2009 US Open]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tennis.com/pro-game/2018/03/juan-martin-del-potrao-roger-federer-2018-indian-wells-final/72797/ |title=With Indian Wells win over Federer, del Potro gives ATP a needed edge |date=18 March 2018 |publisher=Tennis.com |access-date=5 April 2018 |archive-date=6 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406041428/http://www.tennis.com/pro-game/2018/03/juan-martin-del-potrao-roger-federer-2018-indian-wells-final/72797/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Del Potro continued his successful run at the [[2018 Miami Open – Men's singles|Miami Open]], beating Robin Haase, Kei Nishikori and [[Filip Krajinović]], before prevailing in a grueling match against Milos Raonic, reaching the semifinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro grinds down Raonic in Miami, Isner also advances |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-tennis-miami-men-idUKKBN1H439T |website=Reuters |date=28 March 2018}}</ref> His 15-match win streak ended as he was defeated by eventual champion John Isner.<ref>{{cite web |title=John Isner vs. Juan Martin del Potro {{!}} Miami 2018 |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/scores/match-stats/archive/2018/403/ms003 |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Isner hits Del Potro off the court to reach Miami final |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-isner-miami-2018-friday-sf |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=30 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Nina Pantic |title=Isner "keeps pounding" his way through Miami |url=https://www.tennis.com/baseline/articles/isner-keeps-pounding-his-way-through-miami |website=Tennis.com |date=30 March 2018}}</ref>

Del Potro returned to the courts in early May for the clay court season, although his first results were lackluster. After starting the [[2018 Mutua Madrid Open – Men's singles|Madrid Open]] with a solid victory against Bosnian [[Damir Džumhur]] in the second round, he was upset by qualifier [[Dušan Lajović]] in three sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lajovic stuns Delpo in upset of the week |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-anderson-madrid-2018-thursday-1 |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=10 May 2018}}</ref> In his next tournament in [[2018 Italian Open – Men's singles|Rome]], del Potro defeated rising star [[Stefanos Tsitsipas]] before retiring against David Goffin in the next round due to a groin injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro suffers groin strain at Italian Open |url=https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/32455/11378377/juan-martin-del-potro-suffers-groin-strain-at-italian-open |website=Sky Sports |date=20 May 2018}}</ref> His participation at the [[2018 French Open – Men's singles|French Open]] was in doubt but he recovered in time and entered the tournament as the fifth seed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro doubt for Roland Garros |url=https://www.france24.com/en/20180519-del-potro-doubt-roland-garros |website=France24 |date=19 May 2018}}</ref> Following victories against French players [[Nicolas Mahut]] and [[Julien Benneteau]], he defeated 31st seed [[Albert Ramos Viñolas]] and world No. 10, John Isner, en route to a quarterfinal clash against world No. 4 and frequent rival, Marin Čilić. After an intense match, in which he had an argument with a fan who supposedly heckled him, Del Potro defeated Čilić in four sets and reached the semifinals, the first time since [[2009 French Open – Men's singles|2009]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Sarah Edworthy |title=Ddel Potro reaches first RG semi-final in nine years |url=https://www.rolandgarros.com/en-us/article/roland-garros-2018-juan-martin-del-potro-overcomes-marin-cilic |website=Roland-Garros |date=7 June 2018}}</ref> He then lost to ten-times French Open champion Rafael Nadal in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Kevin Mitchell |title=Rafael Nadal dominates Del Potro to set up French Open final with Thiem |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/jun/08/french-open-semi-final-rafael-nadal-dominic-thiem-juan-martin-del-potro-marco-cecchinato |website=The Guardian |date=8 June 2018}}</ref> His run to the semifinals ensured that, for the first time since February 2014, Del Potro would return to his career-best ranking of world No. 4.<ref name="wimbledon2018">{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro: Fourth round |url=https://www.wimbledon.com/en_GB/news/articles/2018-07-10/2018-07-10_juan_martin_del_potro_fourth_round.html |website=Wimbledon |publisher=AELTC |date=10 July 2018 |quote=I'm No. 4 in the world, which is my highest ranking in my career.}}</ref>

At Wimbledon, Del Potro defeated [[Peter Gojowczyk]], [[Feliciano López|Feliciano Lopez]] and [[Benoît Paire]], before a long four set win over 2 days against [[Gilles Simon]].<ref name="wimbledon2018"/> World No. 1 Rafael Nadal defeated him in five sets in the quarters after del Potro had led two sets to one.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Kevin Mitchell |title=Rafael Nadal shows his warrior spirit to beat Del Potro and reach semi-finals |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/jul/11/rafael-nadal-del-potro-wimbledon-semi-finals |website=The Guardian |date=11 July 2018}}</ref> Del Potro then competed at the [[2018 Los Cabos Open – Singles|Los Cabos Open]], where he reached the final but lost to second-seeded [[Fabio Fognini]] in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro falls to Fabio Fognini in Los Cabos final |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/tennis/atp-los-cabos/2018/fabio-fognini-takes-title-in-los-cabos-open_sto6874511/story.shtml |website=[[TNT Sports]] |date=5 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=ATP roundup: Fognini stuns del Potro for Los Cabos title |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-tennis-roundup/atp-roundup-fognini-stuns-del-potro-for-los-cabos-title-idUSKBN1KQ05L |website=Reuters |date=5 August 2018}}</ref> Del Potro moved up to a new career-high ranking of world No. 3 as of the week of 13 August.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Erin Maher |title=Juan Martin del Potro healthy, confident in return to NY |url=https://www.usopen.org/en_US/news/articles/2018-08-24/juan_martin_del_potro_healthy_confident_in_return_to_ny.html |website=US Open |date=24 August 2018}}</ref> Del Potro was seeded fourth at [[2018 Western & Southern Open|Cincinnati]], defeating [[Chung Hyeon]] and [[Nick Kyrgios]] before falling to David Goffin in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro downs Kyrgios in Cincinnati |url=https://www.tennis.com.au/news/2018/08/18/del-potro-beats-kyrgios-cincinnati |website=Tennis Australia |date=18 August 2018}}</ref>

Entering the [[2018 US Open (tennis)|US Open]] seeded third, del Potro reached the quarterfinals without dropping a set, defeating [[Donald Young (tennis)|Donald Young]], [[Denis Kudla]], 31st seed Fernando Verdasco, and 20th seed [[Borna Ćorić]]. He then faced 11th seed John Isner, defeating him in four sets to reach his second consecutive US Open semifinal, where he faced top seed and defending champion Rafael Nadal in a rematch of the previous year's semifinal. Nadal retired from the match due to a knee injury after del Potro took the first two sets.<ref name="2018_usopen_nadal">{{cite web |author1=Jonathan Jurejko |title=Juan Martin del Potro into US Open final as Rafael Nadal retires injured |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/45455869 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 September 2018}}</ref> With this victory, del Potro advanced to his second Grand Slam final, nine years after his [[2009 US Open (tennis)|2009 US Open]] triumph. He was defeated by two-time champion Novak Djokovic in three straight sets.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Kevin Mitchell |title=Novak Djokovic powers past Juan Martín del Potro to win third US Open |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/sep/09/novak-djokovic-juan-martin-del-potro-us-open-mens-final-match-report |website=The Guardian |date=10 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Arthur Kapetanakis |title=Novak Djokovic defeats Juan Martin del Potro for 14th Grand Slam title |url=https://www.usopen.org/en_US/news/articles/2018-09-09/2018-09-09_novak_djokovic_defeats_juan_martin_del_potro_for_14th_grand_slam_title.html |website=US Open |date=9 September 2018}}</ref>

Del Potro entered the [[2018 China Open – Men's singles|China Open]] in October as the top seed. He defeated [[Albert Ramos Viñolas]], Karen Khachanov, [[Filip Krajinović]], and reached the final without dropping a set after [[Fabio Fognini]] withdrew before the semifinal. He faced unseeded [[Nikoloz Basilashvili]] in the final, losing in two sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Georgia's Nikoloz Basilashvili downs Argentina's Juan Martin del Potro in China Open final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/45775959 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Tennis news – Nikoloz Basilashvili stuns ailing Juan Martin Del Potro for Beijing title |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/tennis/atp-beijing/2018/tennis-news-nikoloz-basilashvili-stuns-ailing-juan-martin-del-potro-for-beijing-title_sto6963102/story.shtml |website=[[TNT Sports]] |date=7 October 2018}}</ref> He then competed in the [[2018 Shanghai Rolex Masters|Shanghai Masters]] seeded third. He defeated [[Richard Gasquet]] and faced 13th seed Borna Ćorić in the third round, narrowly dropping the first set before he retired due to a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Coric makes Shanghai QF after Delpo retires |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/coric-del-potro-shanghai-2018-thursday |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=11 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Niko Vercelletto |title=Del Potro takes heavy fall, hurts knee in Shanghai |url=https://www.tennis.com/baseline/articles/del-potro-takes-heavy-fall-hurts-knee-in-shanghai |website=Tennis.com |date=14 October 2018}}</ref> This injury forced his withdrawal from the rest of the season, including the [[2018 ATP Finals|ATP Finals]], for which he had qualified for the first time since 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro secures return to Nitto ATP Finals |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-nitto-atp-finals-2018-qualification |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=3 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Nishikori replaces del Potro at 2018 Nitto ATP Finals |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/nishikori-nitto-atp-finals-2018-joins-field |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=3 November 2018}}</ref>

===2019–2021: Continued injuries===
Del Potro's injury lingered into the [[2019 ATP Tour|2019 season]], forcing him to withdraw from the [[2019 Australian Open|Australian Open]]. He made his comeback at the [[2019 Delray Beach Open|Delray Beach Open]] in February where he reached the quarterfinals, losing to [[Mackenzie McDonald]] in three sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Delray Beach Open: Juan Martin del Potro reaches quarter-finals in Florida |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/47328744 |website=BBC Sport |date=22 February 2019}}</ref> Still not having recovered from injury, Del Potro chose not to defend his titles in [[2019 Abierto Mexicano Telcel|Acapulco]] and [[2019 BNP Paribas Open|Indian Wells]], withdrawing from both tournaments. Playing in his first tournament back at the [[2019 Mutua Madrid Open|Madrid Open]], del Potro lost his first match to [[Laslo Djere]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Djere stops Del Potro in his tracks |url=https://mutuamadridopen.com/en/djere-stops-del-potro-in-his-tracks/ |website=Mutua Madrid Open |date=8 May 2019}}</ref> He then played in Rome and secured wins against David Goffin, who had a 3–1 lead over him before the match, and [[Casper Ruud]]. He failed to convert two match points in a second set tiebreaker to ultimately lose his quarterfinal against world No. 1 Novak Djokovic over a three-hour match.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Jonathon Braden |title=Djokovic Saves 2 MP Against Del Potro In Rome |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/djokovic-del-potro-rome-2019-friday-qf |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=17 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Steve Tignor |title=Djokovic saves 2 match points, tops del Potro in surprise Rome classic |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/djokovic-saves-2-match-points-tops-del-potro-in-surprise-rome-classic |website=Tennis.com |date=17 May 2019}}</ref>

At the [[2019 French Open – Men's singles|2019 French Open]], del Potro was seeded eighth. After wins in the first three rounds against [[Nicolás Jarry]], [[Yoshihito Nishioka]] and [[Jordan Thompson (tennis)|Jordan Thompson]] respectively he lost in the fourth round to tenth-seeded [[Karen Khachanov]] in four sets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Khachanov beats Del Potro to reach first Slam QF; guarantees Top 10 spot |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-khachanov-roland-garros-2019-monday |website=ATP Tour |publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) |date=3 June 2019}}</ref> In his first grass-court tournament of the season at [[2019 Queen's Club Championships – Singles|Queen's Club]], del Potro suffered another career-threatening injury when he fractured his kneecap in his first round match against [[Denis Shapovalov]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/tennis/juan-martin-del-potro-career-over-injury-queens-club-how-long-a8969756.html |title=Juan Martin Del Potro admits career could be over after latest injury nightmare |date=2019-06-21 |website=The Independent |language=en |access-date=2019-06-27 |archive-date=22 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190622121112/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/tennis/juan-martin-del-potro-career-over-injury-queens-club-how-long-a8969756.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

Del Potro did not play any professional tennis from June 2019 at Queen's Club until 2022 at the Argentina Open. He underwent four right knee surgeries (June 2019, January 2020, August 2020 and March 2021)<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro – Bio |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/players/juan-martin-del-potro/d683/bio |website=ATP Tour |publisher=ATP Tour, Inc. |access-date=14 January 2021 |archive-date=21 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121123856/https://www.atptour.com/en/players/juan-martin-del-potro/d683/bio |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro to have more knee surgery, still hopeful for Olympics |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-delpotro-idUSKBN2BE33J |website=Reuters |date=22 March 2021}}</ref> and withdrew from the [[2020 Tokyo Olympics|Tokyo Olympics]] in July 2021.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Dzevad Mesic |title=Juan Martin del Potro out of Tokyo Olympics |url=https://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/ATP_Tennis/99252/juan-martin-del-potro-out-of-tokyo-olympics/ |website=Tennis World USA |date=23 June 2021}}</ref> At the [[2021 US Open (tennis)|2021 US Open]], del Potro reported that his knee was getting better, he had picked up training on the court again and hoped to be ready to play on the tour within a couple of months.<ref>{{cite web |title=Juan Martin del Potro gives injury update, praises Novak Djokovic during US Open visit |url=https://www.usopen.org/en_US/news/articles/2021-09-07/juan_martin_del_potro_gives_injury_update_praises_novak_djokovic_during_us_open_visit.html |publisher=US Open |date=7 September 2021 |access-date=9 September 2021 |archive-date=8 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210908124536/https://www.usopen.org/en_US/news/articles/2021-09-07/juan_martin_del_potro_gives_injury_update_praises_novak_djokovic_during_us_open_visit.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

===2022: Return to professional tennis, potential retirement===
On 31 January, it was announced that Del Potro will make his return to professional tennis at the Argentina Open, where he accepted a wildcard. He also accepted a wildcard to play the Rio Open.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-buenos-aires-rio-de-janeiro-2022-wild-cards |title=Del Potro Accepts Wild Cards Into Buenos Aires & Rio de Janeiro |website=ATP Tour |date=January 31, 2022 |access-date=31 January 2022 |archive-date=31 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220131200704/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/del-potro-buenos-aires-rio-de-janeiro-2022-wild-cards |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 5 February, Del Potro stated in a press conference that he would likely retire after the [[2022 Argentina Open|Argentina Open]]. He cited ongoing knee pain due to an injury as a reason behind the potential retirement, and said that his return is "maybe more of a farewell than a comeback".<ref>{{cite news |title='This is farewell' – Juan Martin del Potro says he's likely to retire after Argentina Open |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/60273217 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 February 2022 |access-date=5 February 2022 |archive-date=5 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205210217/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/60273217 |url-status=live}}</ref> Del Potro lost in the first round of the Argentina Open to [[Federico Delbonis]], and again hinted at retirement in the post-match interview.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/60315243 |title=Juan Martin del Potro loses on return and hints at farewell |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 February 2022 |access-date=9 February 2022 |archive-date=9 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209212126/https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/60315243 |url-status=live}}</ref> He withdrew from the [[2022 Rio Open]] on 11 February.<ref>{{cite web |title=Del Potro pulls out of Rio Open amid retirement talk |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/del-potro-pulls-out-rio-open-amid-retirement-talk-2022-02-11/ |publisher=Reuters |date=11 February 2022 |access-date=11 February 2022}}</ref> Del Potro has not played any matches since; he dropped out of the singles rankings on 20 June, as well as the doubles rankings on 9 May.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 June 2022 |title=Llegó el día: Juan Martín del Potro desapareció del ranking |language=es |publisher=ESPN |url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/tenis/nota/_/id/10534180/llego-el-dia-juan-martin-del-potro-desaparecio-del-ranking |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref>

===2023–2024: Failed comeback at the US Open, farewell exhibition match===
In March, he stated that he would begin training for a potential return at the 2023 US Open.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurosport.co.uk/tennis/us-open/2023/juan-martin-del-potro-will-start-training-as-he-eyes-us-open-comeback-at-most-special-tournament-for_sto9532665/story.shtml |title=Juan Martin del Potro 'will start training' as he eyes US Open comeback at 'most special tournament for me' |date=27 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tennismajors.com/atp/del-potro-to-resume-training-with-hopes-of-playing-us-open-669725.html |title=Del Potro to resume training with US Open on mind |date=26 March 2023}}</ref> In August, he announced that he would not be able to compete in the tournament, due to his physical state.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-16 |title=Ailing del Potro won't make US Open return |url=https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/38204823/juan-martin-del-potro-make-us-open-return-due-health |access-date=2023-09-08 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://tennis-infinity.com/atp/juan-martin-del-potro-explains-why-he-wont-make-comeback-at-2023-us-open|title=Juan Martin Del Potro Explains Why He Won't Make Comeback At 2023 US Open|publisher=Tennis Infinity|accessdate=4 December 2024}}</ref>

Del Potro took part in a farewell exhibition match titled 'The Last Challenge' against Novak Djokovic in Buenos Aires on 1 December 2024. In front of 15,000 spectators, he won in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/articles/clyjn18z8z4o|title=Del Potro pays emotional goodbye to tennis|publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=4 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/tennis/novak-djokovic-roger-federer-pay-tribute-juan-martin-del-potro-emotional-farewell-example_sto20059200/story.shtml|title='Everyone loves him' – Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer pay tribute to Juan Martin del Potro at emotional farewell|publisher=[[TNT Sports]]|access-date=4 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/story/tennis-juan-martin-del-potro-bids-farewell-to-tennis-wins-final-match-vs-novak-djokovic-2643343-2024-12-02|title=Juan Martin del Potro bids farewell to tennis, wins final match vs Novak Djokovic|publisher=India Today|accessdate=4 December 2024}}</ref>

==Playing style==
Del Potro was an [[Tennis strategy#Offensive or aggressive baseliner|offensive baseliner]] with a very powerful [[Serve (tennis)|serve]] and heavy [[groundstroke]]s,<ref>{{cite news |last=Newman |first=Paul |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/tennis/murray-insists-on-doing-the-talking-against-del-potro-917091.html |title=Murray insists on doing the talking against del Potro |work=The Independent |date=3 September 2008 |access-date=15 September 2009 |location=London |archive-date=6 April 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090406010246/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/tennis/murray-insists-on-doing-the-talking-against-del-potro-917091.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Johnson |first=William |url=http://www.thenational.ae/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20090811/SPORT/708109902/1028 |title=Del Potro turning up the heat |work=The National |date=10 August 2009 |access-date=15 September 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014174922/http://www.thenational.ae/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20090811%2FSPORT%2F708109902%2F1028 |archive-date=14 October 2013 |df=dmy-all}}</ref> using his notably powerful forehand to push his opponents deep into or off the court. His [[forehand]] was one of his main strengths and was one the most powerful in the game, capable of frequently generating speeds more than 160 km/h.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/tennis/federer_stunned_by_del_potro_RISV6Ozs3q83twZNjOOb8K |title=Federer stunned by del Potro |work=New York Post |date=14 September 2009 |access-date=23 September 2009 |archive-date=23 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090923005500/http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/tennis/federer_stunned_by_del_potro_RISV6Ozs3q83twZNjOOb8K |url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:Juan Martín del Potro at the 2009 US Open 02.jpg|thumb|250px|Del Potro hits a forehand.]]
It was widely considered among the top three best forehands on tour by fellow players and analysts, alongside [[Roger Federer]] and [[Rafael Nadal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/Rafael_Nadal/47113/rafael-nadal-if-you-let-del-potro-hit-strong-forehand-you-are-dead-/|title=Rafael Nadal: 'If you let del Potro hit strong forehand, you are DEAD'|date=7 September 2017 |access-date=14 May 2018|archive-date=14 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180514142110/http://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/Rafael_Nadal/47113/rafael-nadal-if-you-let-del-potro-hit-strong-forehand-you-are-dead-/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/Rafael_Nadal/54798/rafael-nadal-drops-unexpected-praise-on-roger-federer/|title=Rafael Nadal drops unexpected praise on Roger Federer|date=13 May 2018 |access-date=14 May 2018|archive-date=14 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180514142155/http://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/Rafael_Nadal/54798/rafael-nadal-drops-unexpected-praise-on-roger-federer/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tennisnow.com/Blogs/NET-POSTS/September-2017-(1)/Federer-Names-Best-Forehand.aspx|title=Federer Names Best Forehand|access-date=14 May 2018|archive-date=14 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180514213607/http://www.tennisnow.com/Blogs/NET-POSTS/September-2017-(1)/Federer-Names-Best-Forehand.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tennis.com/pro-game/2014/01/tomic-del-potro-owns-best-forehand-tour/50198/|title=Tomic: Del Potro has best forehand on tour|access-date=14 May 2018|archive-date=14 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180514141852/http://www.tennis.com/pro-game/2014/01/tomic-del-potro-owns-best-forehand-tour/50198/|url-status=live}}</ref>
